definition_zh: 政治家；从政者；政客（含贬义时指善于权术、重许诺轻原则的人）
definition_en: a person who holds or seeks public office and lives by political activity, sometimes with the implication of manoeuvring rather than principle
core_image: 集市广场上，竞选者站在木箱上讲话，向每个伸出手的人逐一握过去
scene: 集市广场上，竞选者站在木箱上讲完承诺，又向每个伸出手的人逐一握过去。The politician promised to fix the drains before the winter rains came.
sceneCN: 这里指「担任或谋求公职的从政者」，对应第 1 个义项：以公职身份参与政治的人；句意为这位从政者承诺在冬雨到来之前修好排水。画面要点：木箱讲台、人群、握手动作；对应第 1 个义项。

政客（含贬义，指工于权术、重私利者）

senses.title: A holder or seeker of public office
senses.definition: a person who occupies an elected or appointed office in government or is running for one
senses.definitionCN: 在政府中担任经选举或任命产生的职位、正在竞选这类职位的人
senses.example: The politician promised to fix the drains before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这位从政者承诺在入冬前修好排水。
senses.why: the suffix marks the practitioner of the activity named by the stem, so the word literally means one who does civic politics.
senses.whyCN: 后缀标记的是词干所指活动的从业者，因此这个词字面上就是一个做城邦政治的人。

senses.title: One who lives by politics as a trade
senses.definition: a person whose income, identity and daily work come from political activity rather than from another profession
senses.definitionCN: 收入、身份与日常工作都来自政治活动、而非另一门职业的人
senses.example: He had been a politician for thirty years and had never held another job.
senses.exampleCN: 他做了三十年从政者，从未干过别的工作。
senses.why: an activity becomes a trade when it supports a life, and the word then carries the neutral sense of a profession.
senses.whyCN: 一项活动一旦能养活一个人，就成了职业，这个词也就带上中性的职业含义。

senses.title: The pejorative reading: a dealer in promises
senses.titleCN: 贬义：只会许诺与算计的人
senses.definition: a person seen as caring more about advantage and image than about doing what is right
senses.definitionCN: 被认为更在意利益与形象、而非把事情做对的人
senses.example: They called him a politician to his face, meaning it as an insult.
senses.exampleCN: 他们当面称他为政客，这词是当侮辱用的。
senses.why: because the trade depends on winning consent, the same word easily slides into a charge of insincerity.
senses.whyCN: 由于这一行依赖赢得同意，同一个词很容易滑向「不真诚」的指责。

senses.title: A local officeholder
senses.definition: a person active in municipal or county government, closer to ward business than to national debate
senses.definitionCN: 活跃于市镇或县级政府的人，离选区事务比离全国辩论更近
senses.example: A local politician opened the new clinic and stayed for every photograph.
senses.exampleCN: 一位地方从政者为新诊所剪彩，每张合影都不缺席。
senses.why: the scale of office is supplied by an adjective, and local names the rung nearest to voters.
senses.whyCN: 职位层级由形容词补出，而「地方的」正指离选民最近的那一级。

senses.title: A party figure who brokers support
senses.definition: a person whose standing rests on organising votes and alliances within a party rather than on public speaking
senses.definitionCN: 地位靠组织党内票源与结盟、而非靠公开演讲的人
senses.example: The party politician settled the nomination in a back room.
senses.exampleCN: 这位党务人物在后台一间屋子里敲定了提名。
senses.why: inside a party the work is counting and trading support, so the word shifts from office to organization.
senses.whyCN: 在政党内部，工作是数票与换取支持，于是这个词从「职位」转向「组织」。

senses.title: A skilled operator in any institution
senses.titleCN: 任何机构里善于运作的人
senses.definition: in extended use, a colleague who wins by alliance and timing inside a firm, school or association
senses.definitionCN: 引申用法：在企业、学校或团体内部靠结盟与时点取胜的同事
senses.example: The department head was a politician long before he held a title.
senses.exampleCN: 这位系主任在拿到头衔之前很久就是个政治人物了。
senses.why: the pattern of allies and rivals repeats at any scale, so the label is borrowed wherever influence is scarce.
senses.whyCN: 盟友与对手的格局在任何规模上都会重演，因此只要影响力稀缺，这个标签就会被借去用。

senses.title: The older reading: one versed in statecraft
senses.titleCN: 旧义：精通治国之术的人
senses.definition: in earlier usage, a person learned in the theory and practice of governing, close to what we now call a statesman
senses.definitionCN: 较早的用法中指通晓治国理论与实务的人，接近今天所说的政治家
senses.example: Sixteenth-century writers praised the politician who could hold a restless city.
senses.exampleCN: 十六世纪的作者称赞那种能稳住躁动城邦的治国者。
senses.why: when the word entered English it named knowledge of civic affairs, and the pejorative tone came later with mass electoral politics.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时指通晓城邦事务的学问，贬义色彩是后来随大众选举政治才出现的。

senses.title: Abstract: one who turns influence into office
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把影响力换成职位的人
senses.definition: in general use, anyone who converts personal influence into formal authority over a group
senses.definitionCN: 泛指把个人影响力换成对某个群体的正式权威的人
senses.example: In any club, the politician is the member who knows when to call the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何社团里，政治人物都是那个知道何时该提请表决的成员。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the exchange of influence for authority and lets the state and the ballot box fall away.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只留下「以影响力换权威」这一交换，国家与票箱都退出了画面。

intro.en: Politician is an English noun built on the Greek-derived stem of political with the person suffix -ian, and its meaning has shifted from learned statecraft to electoral profession. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: politician 是英语用 political 的希腊来源词干加表人后缀构成的名词，其含义从「治国之学」演变为「选举职业」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polis meant a city-state and its citizen body; its deeper origin is not established, and the pre-Greek suggestion is only a hypothesis.
items.cn: polis 指城邦及其公民总体；它更深的来源未得到证明，前希腊语来源的说法只是假说。

items.en: Politikos meant 'of citizens, civic, fit for governing', and the derived art of civic management was called politike.
items.cn: politikos 意为「公民的、城邦的、适于治理的」，由它派生的治城之术称为 politike。

items.en: Latin borrowed politicus for civil and state affairs, and medieval writers used politica for the study of the state.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 politicus 用于民政与国家事务，中世纪作者用 politica 指对国家的研究。

items.en: The English noun first meant a person skilled in the science of government, often in a neutral or approving tone.
items.cn: 这个英语名词最初指精通治国之学的人，语气常为中性甚至赞许。

items.en: As parties and mass electorates grew in the nineteenth century, the word settled into its modern sense of a person who lives by winning office, and the disparaging tone followed.
items.cn: 十九世纪政党与大众选民兴起后，这个词固定为「以赢得职位为业的人」这一现代义，贬义语气也随之而来。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same stem that are easily mistaken for the person; group two holds labels for people in public life with different shades of approval.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干、容易被误当成本词的词；第二组是评价色彩不同的公共人物称谓。

entries.definition: The activity or field itself; a politician is the person who practices it.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动或领域本身；politician 则是从事这一活动的人。

entries.definition: Describing what belongs to government or power; it cannot stand for the person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于政府或权力的事物；不能用来指人。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning shrewd and tactful, not a noun for an officeholder.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为精明得体的，不是指公职人员的名词。

entries.definition: A course of action adopted by a body; it sounds close but names a document or a rule, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 机构采用的行动方针；读音相近，但指的是文件或规则，不是人。

entries.definition: A senior figure respected for judgement in public affairs; the word is almost always a compliment, unlike politician.
entries.definitionCN: 因公共事务上的判断力而受尊敬的人物；这个词几乎总是褒义，与 politician 不同。

entries.definition: A neutral term for anyone currently holding a post; it says nothing about how the post was won or used.
entries.definitionCN: 对现任职位者的中性说法；不涉及职位如何得到或如何使用。

entries.definition: A person who makes laws in a parliament; a politician may serve in an executive post and never vote on a bill.
entries.definitionCN: 在议会中制定法律的人；政治人物也可能担任行政职务，从不参与法案表决。

entries.definition: A leader who wins support by playing on fear and prejudice; it is far harsher than the pejorative use of politician.
entries.definitionCN: 靠煽动恐惧与偏见来赢得支持的领袖；比 politician 的贬义用法严厉得多。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The stem means civic, and the person suffix marks the one who practices civic business for a living.
normal.cn: 词干意为「城邦的」，表人后缀标记的正是以城邦事务为业的人。

normal.en: The family runs political, politically, politics, polity and politicize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括政治的、在政治上、政治、政体与使政治化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the tone: a seasoned politician is neutral, a corrupt politician is a charge.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示语气：老练的从政者是中性的，腐败的政客则是控诉。

normal.en: The word entered English meaning a student of statecraft and only later became the electoral professional.
normal.cn: 这个词进入英语时指治国之学的研习者，后来才变成选举职业者。

normal.en: The approving counterpart is statesman, which is almost never used as an insult.
normal.cn: 褒义对应词是 statesman，那个词几乎从不被当作侮辱使用。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden crate used as a platform, with hands reaching up from the crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只木箱被当作讲台，人群中有手不断伸上来。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook of names, each marked with a promise and a date.
abstract.cn: 想象一本写满姓名的册子，每个名字旁都记着一句承诺和一个日期。

abstract.en: Picture a back room where two people count votes on their fingers before a public vote.
abstract.cn: 想象后台一间屋子里，两个人在公开表决前掰着手指清点票数。

examples.en: The politician spent the morning at three different factory gates.
examples.cn: 这位从政者一上午跑了三个工厂门口。

examples.en: Voters said they trusted the engineer more than the politician.
examples.cn: 选民说他们更信任那位工程师，而不是那位政客。

examples.en: Every politician in the county knew the bridge budget by heart.
examples.cn: 县里每一位从政者都把桥梁预算记得滚瓜烂熟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「城邦事务 + 做事的人」——以摆平众人之事为职业的人 → 从政者

root: politician 由 political 的希腊来源词干加表示「从事者」的表人后缀构成；词干出自希腊 politikos「公民的、城邦的」，源头 polis「城邦」，经拉丁 politicus 与法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses slide along one career: the officeholder, the professional, the promise-dealer, the local figure, the party broker, the institutional operator, the old student of statecraft, and finally anyone trading influence for authority.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条职业线滑动：任职者、以此为业者、兜售承诺者、地方人物、党内撮合者、机构里的运作人、旧义中的治国学者，最后是把影响力换成权威的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker on a crate, shaking every hand within reach.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在木箱上的讲话者，把够得到的手都握一遍。

branches.en: OFFICE: the plain reading, a person who holds or seeks a public post.
branches.cn: 职位：最朴素的读法，即担任或谋求公职的人。

branches.en: TRADE AND SCEPTICISM: once politics is a livelihood, the same word can be neutral about the job or doubtful about the person.
branches.cn: 职业与怀疑：政治一旦成为生计，同一个词既可就职业作中性描述，也可就人品表示怀疑。

branches.en: SCALE AND PARTY: the rung nearest the voter and the back-room broker are two ends of the same ladder.
branches.cn: 层级与党派：离选民最近的那一级与后台的撮合者，是同一条梯子的两端。

branches.en: ANYWHERE AND EARLIER: the operator appears in any institution, and the older reading still honours the student of statecraft.
branches.cn: 无处不在与更早用法：运作人出现在任何机构里，而旧读法仍尊重治国之学的研习者。

branches.en: EXCHANGE: strip the state away and what remains is influence turned into authority.
branches.cn: 交换：把国家抽走，剩下的就是影响力被换成权威。

intro.en: Politician is a Greek-derived stem plus a Latin-derived person suffix, and both halves are shared with a large English family.
intro.cn: politician 是希腊来源的词干加拉丁来源的表人后缀，两半都与一个庞大的英语词族共享。

latinIntro.en: Latin politicus stands behind the stem, and the person suffix reached English through French forms ending in -ien.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 politicus 是这一词干的来源，表人后缀则经法语中同类的表人形式进入英语。

items.example: Latin carried the stem into learned use.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这一词干带入学术用法。

items.example: The suffix marks the practitioner rather than the theorist.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记从业者，而非理论者。
这个形容词描述这一领域。

items.example: Politics is the practice, not the person.

items.exampleCN: 这场争端一周之内就被政治化了。

senses.title: The activity of governing and competing for power
senses.titleCN: 治理与争夺权力的活动
senses.definition: the activity by which groups decide who holds public authority and how it is used
senses.definitionCN: 各群体决定公共权力归谁掌握、如何使用的活动
senses.example: Politics decides who gets the water and who waits.
senses.exampleCN: 政治决定谁能先得水、谁只能等。
senses.why: the Greek root names the city and its citizens, so the word began as the business of the civic body rather than of private life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的希腊词根指城邦及其公民，因此它最初指公民集体的事务，而非私人生活。

senses.title: A person's views or affiliation
senses.titleCN: 个人的政治见解或党派立场
senses.definition: the set of beliefs a person holds about how society and government should be run
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对社会与政府应如何运转所持的一整套信念
senses.example: Her politics are greener than her party's platform.
senses.exampleCN: 她的政治立场比本党纲领更偏环保。
senses.why: beliefs about governing are held by individuals, so the plural noun came to mean one person's stance and can take a plural verb in this sense.
senses.whyCN: 关于治理的信念由个人持有，因此这个以复数形式收尾的名词转指个人的立场，作此义时可用复数动词。

senses.title: The profession and world of politicians
senses.definition: the career, workplace and daily life of those who hold or seek public office
senses.definitionCN: 担任或谋求公职者的职业、职场与日常处境
senses.example: He went into politics after running the city hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 他管过市立医院之后进入了政界。
senses.why: an activity that occupies a career becomes a place one enters, hence phrases about going into or leaving politics.
senses.whyCN: 一项活动一旦占据一份职业，就变成可以走进去的场所，于是有了进入政界、退出政界这类说法。

senses.title: The academic subject
senses.titleCN: 政治学（学科名，英式常用）
senses.definition: the study of government and political behaviour as a university discipline
senses.definitionCN: 在大学里把政府与政治行为作为研究对象的学科
senses.example: She read politics before turning to law.
senses.exampleCN: 她先读政治学，之后转行学法。
senses.why: the Greek title of a book on civic affairs became the name of the school subject that studies them.
senses.whyCN: 一本论城邦事务的希腊书名，后来成了研究这些事务的学科名称。

senses.title: Manoeuvring inside an organization
senses.definition: the informal struggle for influence and favour within a workplace, club or family
senses.definitionCN: 在工作场所、团体或家庭内部为影响力与青睐而进行的非正式争夺
senses.example: Office politics kept the best engineer off the project.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室里的权术让最好的工程师进不了这个项目。
senses.why: the patterns of alliance and rivalry repeat at any scale, so the word is borrowed wherever a small group allocates scarce goods.
senses.whyCN: 结盟与对立的方式在任何规模上都会重演，因此只要小群体分配稀缺之物，这个词就会被借去用。

senses.title: Public contest over policy and office
senses.titleCN: 围绕政策与职位的公共竞争
senses.definition: the open competition of parties, campaigns and interest groups over what government should do
senses.definitionCN: 政党、竞选活动与利益团体围绕政府应当做什么而展开的公开竞争
senses.example: The politics of the budget turned on two marginal seats.
senses.exampleCN: 预算的政治角力集中在两个边缘选区上。
senses.why: when conflict is public and organised, the word names the contest itself rather than the general activity.
senses.whyCN: 当冲突公开且有组织时，这个词指的是竞争本身，而不是笼统的活动。

senses.title: The arena or system as a whole
senses.titleCN: 政治舞台与制度环境的总称
senses.definition: the whole institutional setting in which authority is won, used and lost
senses.definitionCN: 权力被赢得、使用与失去的整套制度环境
senses.example: Trust in politics fell after the expenses scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 报销丑闻之后，人们对政治这一套制度的信任下降了。
senses.why: the activity and the setting are named by one word, so the noun can stand for the entire arena in which the activity happens.
senses.whyCN: 活动与场所用同一个词表示，因此这个名词也能指活动发生的整个场域。

senses.title: Abstract: the negotiation of collective interests
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：集体利益的协商过程
senses.definition: in general use, any process by which a group with diverging interests reaches a workable decision
senses.definitionCN: 泛指利益分歧的群体达成可行决定的任何过程
senses.example: There is politics in every committee that must divide a budget.
senses.exampleCN: 凡是要分预算的委员会，都有政治。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the settling of divergent interests and lets the state and the ballot drop away.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只留下「摆平分歧利益」这层意思，国家与选票则退出了画面。

intro.en: Politics goes back through French and Latin to the Greek title of Aristotle's book on civic affairs, built on the Greek word for a city. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: politics 经法语与拉丁语上溯到亚里士多德论城邦事务那本书的希腊书名，其词根是希腊语中表示「城邦」的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polis meant a city-state and the citizen body that made it; its deeper origin is not established, and the suggestion of a pre-Greek source is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: polis 指城邦以及构成城邦的公民总体；它更深的来源未得到证明，关于其源自前希腊语层的说法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Polites meant a citizen, one who belongs to the polis and shares in its decisions, and from it came the adjective politikos 'of citizens, civic'.
items.cn: politēs 指公民，即属于城邦并参与其决定的人；由它产生形容词 politikos「公民的、城邦的」。

items.en: Ta politika meant 'the things concerning the city', the title of Aristotle's treatise on the government of states, and it named civic affairs rather than party strife.
items.cn: ta politika 意为「与城邦有关的事务」，是亚里士多德论国家治理那部书的书名，所指为公民事务，而非党派争斗。

items.en: Medieval Latin politica was coined from the Greek title to name the study of the state, and it passed through French into English in the late fifteenth century.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 politica 依那个希腊书名造出，用来指对国家的研究，并在十五世纪晚期经法语进入英语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word spread to party competition, then to the internal manoeuvring of any institution, and finally to 'the politics of' almost any activity.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词先扩展到党派竞争，再指任何机构内部的权术，最后出现「某事背后的政治」这种几乎可用于一切活动的说法。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Greek city root that are easily confused with politics; group two holds terms for governing that do not carry the competitive sense.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「城邦」词根、容易与 politics 混淆的词；第二组是表示治理、但不含竞争意味的术语。

entries.definition: A settled course of action adopted by a government or firm; politics is the struggle that produces or blocks a policy.
entries.definitionCN: 政府或机构采用的既定行动方案；政治则是产生或阻挠某项政策的那场争夺。

entries.definition: A politically organised society viewed as a unit, as in a federal polity; it names the body, not its activity.
entries.definitionCN: 被视作一个单位的有政治组织的社会，如联邦政体；它指共同体本身，而非其活动。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning shrewd and tactful, as in a politic silence; it describes judgement, not government.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词，意为精明得体的，如得体的沉默；它描述判断力，而非政府事务。

entries.definition: A person who holds or seeks office; the practice they live by is politics, and the two are constantly used together.
entries.definitionCN: 担任或谋求公职的人；他们以此谋生的活动就是政治，两者常连用。

entries.definition: The body that exercises authority in a state; government is the machine, while politics is the contest that drives it.
entries.definitionCN: 在国家中行使权力的机构；政府是机器，政治则是驱动机器的那场竞争。

entries.definition: The processes and rules by which decisions are taken, often used of firms and agencies; it is quieter and more technical than politics.
entries.definitionCN: 作出决定所依的流程与规则，常用于企业与机构；它比政治更平实、更技术化。

entries.definition: The art of conducting state affairs, especially foreign policy; it stresses skill and is used of leaders rather than of voters.
entries.definitionCN: 处理国家事务、尤其外交事务的技艺；强调技巧，多用于领导人而非选民。

entries.definition: A neutral term for matters of common concern and the work of dealing with them; it avoids the combative tone of politics.
entries.definitionCN: 对公共事务及其处理工作的中性说法；避开了政治一词的争斗意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is the Greek word for a city-state, so politics is literally the business of the city.
normal.cn: 词根是希腊语中表示城邦的词，所以政治字面上就是城邦的事务。

normal.en: The family runs political, politically, politician, policy, polity and politicize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括政治的、在政治上、政治家、政策、政体与使政治化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: go into politics, office politics, party politics, the politics of reform.
normal.cn: 固定搭配给各义项分类：进入政界、办公室权术、党派政治、改革的政治角力。

normal.en: The word ends in -s but takes a singular verb when it names the activity or the subject.
normal.cn: 这个词虽以表示复数的词尾结尾，但指活动或学科时作单数用。

normal.en: A politician lives by politics; a policy is what the struggle produces.
normal.cn: 政治家靠政治为生；政策则是这场争夺的产物。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd at a water channel, each faction counting heads before the gate is opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人围在水渠边，各派在开闸前清点人数。

abstract.en: Picture a table where five people must split one loaf and nobody wants the smallest piece.
abstract.cn: 想象五个人要分一只面包，谁都不愿拿最小的一块。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor where two groups whisper before entering the same voting hall.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊里两群人在进同一个投票厅之前低声商量。

examples.en: Politics in the region has long followed family lines.
examples.cn: 这个地区的政治长期沿家族脉络运行。

examples.en: She left politics to run a research institute.
examples.cn: 她退出政界，去主持一家研究所。

examples.en: He never discusses his politics at work.
examples.cn: 他在工作时从不谈自己的政治立场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「城邦的事务」——城里人一起商量谁说了算 → 政治

root: politics 经法语与拉丁语出自希腊 ta politika「与城邦有关的事务」，源头是 polis「城邦」与 politēs「公民」；polis 更深来源不确定，前希腊语来源仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses widen from one root: the business of the city becomes a career, then a set of personal beliefs, a university subject, the manoeuvring of any small group, an open electoral contest, the whole arena, and finally any settlement of divergent interests.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一个词根向外扩：城邦的事务先成为一门职业，再成为个人的一整套信念、一门大学学科、任何小团体内部的权术、公开的选举竞争、整个政治场域，最后是任何摆平分歧利益的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: neighbours arguing at a water gate until a rule is agreed.
core.cn: 核心意象：邻人在分水口争论，直到商定一条规则。

branches.en: ROOT ACTIVITY: deciding who holds public authority, the oldest and widest reading.
branches.cn: 根本活动：决定公共权力归谁，这是最古老也最宽的读法。

branches.en: PERSONAL AND PROFESSIONAL: the same word covers what a private person believes and the trade a public person lives by.
branches.cn: 个人与职业：同一个词既指私人的信念，也指公开人物赖以谋生的行业。

branches.en: SUBJECT: the civic business turned into a course of study with its own methods.
branches.cn: 学科：城邦事务被变成一门有自身方法的研究。

branches.en: SCALE OF CONFLICT: quiet manoeuvring in an office and open contest at an election are the same pattern at different sizes.
branches.cn: 冲突的规模：办公室里无声的权术与选举中公开的竞争，是同一种格局的不同尺寸。

branches.en: ARENA AND GENERAL FORM: the whole stage where authority changes hands, then any group dividing what it needs.
branches.cn: 场域与一般形态：先是权力易手的整个舞台，后是任何分配所需之物的群体。

intro.en: Politics rests on a Greek noun for the city and its citizen body, a stem that also builds policy, polity and politician in English.
intro.cn: politics 立在一个表示城邦及其公民总体的希腊名词上，同一词干在英语里还造出政策、政体与政治家。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the Greek stem as politicus and politica, the forms through which the word family reached English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊词干借作 politicus 与 politica，这个词族正是经这两种形式进入英语的。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根指出作出决定的那个单位。

items.example: The citizen, not the subject, is the base of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的基础是公民，而非臣民。

items.example: The adjective described matters that concerned the citizen body.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述与公民总体相关的事务。

items.structure: -ics (Greek suffix naming an art or study)
items.example: The suffix turns civic affairs into a named field.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把城邦事务变成一个有名称的领域。

items.structure: Old French policie, from Latin politica
items.example: Policy is the settled plan, not the contest.
items.exampleCN: 政策是定下来的方案，而非争夺本身。

items.example: A polity can be a city, a state or a federation.
items.exampleCN: 政体可以是一座城、一个国家或一个联邦。

items.example: The budget dispute politicized the school board.
items.exampleCN: 预算争执把校董会政治化了。

items.example: The decision was political rather than technical.
items.exampleCN: 这个决定是政治性的，而非技术性的。

senses.title: A survey of people's opinions
senses.definition: a survey that asks a sample of people what they think about an issue, a product or a candidate
senses.definitionCN: 就某个议题、产品或候选人询问一批抽样对象看法的调查
senses.example: An opinion poll suggested that most voters wanted the plan changed.
senses.exampleCN: 一项民意调查显示，多数选民希望这个方案作出修改。
senses.why: The word first meant a head, then a count of heads; asking people one by one repeats that counting gesture, so a survey inherits the image of ticking off person after person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指「头」，再指「按人头点数」；挨个询问正是重复那个点数的动作，于是民调继承了「一个个人画勾」的画面。

senses.title: The act of voting
senses.definition: the occasion on which people cast votes, usually in the phrase the polls or go to the polls
senses.definitionCN: 人们投下选票的场合，常见于 the polls 或 go to the polls 这样的说法
senses.example: The country went to the polls in the middle of a heat wave.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在一场热浪中举行了投票。
senses.why: Once a poll is a head count, the day when heads are counted becomes the poll itself, and voters are said to go to it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 poll 是「清点人头」，清点人头的那一天本身就成了 poll，选民也就被说成「走向」它。

senses.title: The number of votes recorded
senses.definition: the total of votes won by a candidate or party, or the record of those totals
senses.definitionCN: 某位候选人或政党赢得的票数总和，或记录这些数字的清单
senses.example: The final poll gave the mayor a clear majority.
senses.exampleCN: 最终得票数让市长获得了明显的多数。
senses.why: If the count produces a number, the same noun can name that number, which is how a poll comes to mean the tally a candidate watches all night.
senses.whyCN: 既然清点会得出一个数字，同一个名词就能指那个数字，于是 poll 也指候选人整夜盯着的计票结果。

senses.title: To ask people for their opinions
senses.definition: to question a group of people in order to find out what they think
senses.definitionCN: 为了解一批人的想法而向他们提问
senses.example: She polled her students about which book to read next.
senses.exampleCN: 她就下一本读什么书征求了学生们的意见。
senses.why: The noun names the survey, so the verb names the work of producing one: someone has to go out and put the questions.
senses.whyCN: 名词指调查本身，动词就指做出这项调查的过程：总得有人走出去把问题问出来。

senses.title: To receive a particular number of votes
senses.definition: to win or record a stated number or share of votes in an election
senses.definitionCN: 在选举中获得或记录下某一数字或比例的选票
senses.example: The party polled forty percent of the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 该党获得了四成选票。
senses.why: Because a poll is also the tally, the verb can be used from the other side: a candidate polls the votes that the count gives him.
senses.whyCN: 既然 poll 也指计票结果，动词就能从另一头来用：候选人 poll 到的，就是清点之后记在他名下的票。

intro.en: Poll is a Germanic word for the head that entered English from Dutch; the political senses grew out of counting people head by head, not out of Latin.
intro.cn: poll 是来自荷兰语、意为「头」的日耳曼词；它的政治义项是从「按人头点数」长出来的，与拉丁语无关。

items.en: Middle Dutch pol meant the head or the top of something, and it is generally traced to a Germanic stock rather than to Latin.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 pol 意为头或某物的顶部，一般认为它上溯到日耳曼语来源，而不是拉丁语。

items.en: Middle English polle named the head, and by extension a person counted as one head in a crowd.
items.cn: 中古英语 polle 指头，引申为人群中被当作「一个头」来数的人。

items.en: A poll became a count of heads, then the record of votes at an election, and finally the place where those votes were cast.
items.cn: poll 由「清点人头」变成选举中的计票，再变成投票的场所。

items.en: Newspapers and social research gave the word its survey sense: a sample of heads asked for their opinions.
items.cn: 报纸与社会研究赋予这个词「调查」义：抽出一批人头来问他们的看法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun for a survey, a vote and a tally, and uses the verb both for asking people and for the votes a candidate wins.
items.cn: 现代英语保留名词的「调查、投票、计票」三义，动词则既指去问人，也指候选人赢得的票数。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on this Germanic head word, with one spelling twin from a different root; the near-meaning group gathers words for surveys and voting.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在这个日耳曼「头」词上的形式，并附一个来自别的词根的拼写近邻；近义组收表示「调查」与「投票」的词。

entries.definitionCN: 从事民意调查的人。

entries.definition: The act of voting, or of asking people for their views.

entries.definitionCN: 长杆；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它来自拉丁语中表示「木桩」的词，与「头」这个词无关。

normalIntro.en: The whole family grows from one concrete act: touching a head to count it, whether in a crowd, at a ballot box or on a telephone list.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词都从一个具体动作长出来：点一个头就算一个，不论是在人群里、票箱前还是电话名单上。

normal.en: Poll began as the head, and a poll of the people was a count of heads, which is why voting and surveying share the word.
normal.cn: poll 起初指「头」，a poll of the people 就是清点人头，所以投票与调查共用这个词。

normal.en: Opinion poll puts the noun after the subject it measures, and the phrase is the normal way to name a survey.
normal.cn: opinion poll 把名词放在它所测量的对象之后，是称呼民调最常用的说法。

normal.en: Go to the polls treats the word as a place or event, because the polls are where the counting happens.
normal.cn: go to the polls 把这个词当成地点或事件，因为 the polls 就是清点发生的地方。

normal.en: The verb poll takes a person or group as its object: you poll voters, students or an audience.
normal.cn: 动词 poll 以人或群体作宾语：poll voters、students、an audience。

normal.en: Pollster adds -ster, the old suffix for someone who does a thing, so the word names the person behind the numbers.
normal.cn: pollster 加了 -ster，这个古老后缀表示「做某事的人」，于是这个词指数字背后的人。

abstract.en: A word that moves from head to vote to opinion shows that public voice is always counted in bodies.
abstract.cn: 一个从「头」走到「票」再到「意见」的词说明：公共声音终究是按人头来数的。

abstract.en: The same noun can be the question, the act and the total, because a poll is a circle that closes only when the numbers come back.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词既能是问题、是行为、也是总数，因为民调是一个圈，数字回来才算闭合。

abstract.en: Counting heads is a crude measure, and the word quietly admits it: what is counted is a unit, not a mind.
abstract.cn: 数人头是一种粗糙的度量，这个词也默默承认了这一点：被数的是一个单位，而不是一个头脑。

examples.en: An opinion poll suggested that most voters wanted the plan changed.
examples.cn: 一项民意调查显示，多数选民希望这个方案作出修改。

examples.en: She polled her students about which book to read next.
examples.cn: 她就下一本读什么书征求了学生们的意见。

examples.en: The party polled forty percent of the vote.
examples.cn: 该党获得了四成选票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡欧」——把人头一个个数过去，数出来的是票，问出来的是民调，都是 poll。

root: 中古荷兰语 pol（头顶、头）→ 中古英语 polle（头）→ 按人头计数 → 计票与投票 → 民意调查；属日耳曼来源，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a count of heads; from it come the vote, the tally and the place of voting, and then the modern survey and its verbs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「清点人头」；由此分出投票、计票与投票场所，再长出当代的调查及其动词用法。

senses.title: Harmful matter or energy entering the environment
senses.titleCN: 有害物质或能量进入环境
senses.definition: the act of putting harmful substances or excess energy into air, water or soil
senses.definitionCN: 把有害物质或过量能量放入空气、水体或土壤的行为
senses.example: Pollution had turned the once clear river into a hazard.
senses.exampleCN: 污染把曾经清澈的河变成了危险之地。
senses.why: The word names the act before it names the result: something is put into a medium that was not there before.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先命名动作，再命名结果：某物被放进了本来没有它的介质里。

senses.title: The damaged state of a medium
senses.definition: the condition of air, water or land after harmful matter has entered it
senses.definitionCN: 空气、水或土地在有害物质进入之后所处的状态
senses.example: The lake's pollution was visible as a green scum.
senses.exampleCN: 湖水的污染表现为一层绿色浮沫。
senses.why: English uses the same noun for the act and its result, so pollution can be what was done and what is now there.
senses.whyCN: 英语用同一个名词兼指动作与结果，因此 pollution 既可以是「做了什么」，也可以是「现在有什么」。

senses.title: Air pollution
senses.definition: the presence of smoke, gases or particles in the air at harmful concentrations
senses.definitionCN: 烟、气体或颗粒以有害浓度存在于空气中
senses.example: Winter air pollution settles over the plain and hides the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季的空气污染压在平原上，把群山遮住。
senses.why: Coal smoke made this sense the first and most visible kind of pollution in industrial cities.
senses.whyCN: 煤烟使这个义项成为工业城市里最早、最可见的一种污染。

senses.title: Water pollution
senses.definition: the entry of sewage, chemicals or waste into rivers, lakes, groundwater or the sea
senses.definitionCN: 污水、化学品或废物进入河流、湖泊、地下水或海洋
senses.example: Water pollution from the tannery reached the wells downstream.
senses.exampleCN: 制革厂造成的水污染波及下游的水井。
senses.why: Water carries harm away from the source, so the word stresses the medium that spreads it.
senses.whyCN: 水把危害从源头带走，这个词于是强调传播它的介质。

senses.title: Soil and land pollution
senses.definition: the accumulation of harmful substances in soil, or the degradation of land by waste
senses.definitionCN: 有害物质在土壤中累积，或土地因废物而退化
senses.example: Soil pollution kept the allotments out of use for years.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤污染让这些菜地多年不能使用。
senses.why: Soil holds what air and water deliver, so pollution here is a deposit that stays in place.
senses.whyCN: 土壤承接空气与水送来的东西，这里的污染是留在原地的沉积。

senses.title: Noise, light and heat pollution
senses.definition: excess energy that harms health, wildlife or the quality of a place without adding substance
senses.definitionCN: 过量的能量，不添加物质却危害健康、野生生物或环境品质
senses.example: Light pollution erased the stars above the coastal towns.
senses.exampleCN: 光污染抹去了沿海城镇上空的星空。
senses.why: Modern regulation widened the word to energy, because harm does not require a material to be present.
senses.whyCN: 现代监管把这个词扩展到能量，因为造成危害并不需要有物质在场。

senses.title: Plastic and marine pollution
senses.definition: the accumulation of persistent waste, especially plastics, in oceans and on shores
senses.definitionCN: 持久性废物、尤其是塑料，在海洋与海岸上的累积
senses.example: Marine pollution washed ashore as bottle caps and netting.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋污染以瓶盖和网绳的形式冲上岸。
senses.why: A single material became so dominant that it earned its own use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 单一材料变得如此突出，以至于单独占用了这个词的一种用法。

senses.title: Ritual or moral defilement
senses.definition: the historical sense of making something sacred or pure unclean
senses.definitionCN: 使神圣或纯洁之物变得不洁的旧义
senses.example: The old texts speak of pollution that required a rite of cleansing.
senses.exampleCN: 古籍中说到需要行洁净礼才能解除的玷污。
senses.why: The word entered English as a religious term, and the environmental sense is a later branch of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词以宗教术语进入英语，环境义是同一意象后来分出的枝。

senses.title: Abstract: degradation of information or discourse
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：信息与言论环境的变质
senses.definition: a transferred use for the flooding of a field with false, low-quality or manipulative content
senses.definitionCN: 转指某领域被虚假、低质或操纵性内容淹没
senses.example: Information pollution makes a reliable source harder to find.
senses.exampleCN: 信息污染使可靠来源更难找到。
senses.why: The metaphor preserves the structure: a shared medium is filled with something that lowers its value for everyone.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了结构：共用的介质被填入某物，使它对所有人都贬值。

intro.en: Pollution came to English through French from Latin pollutio, a noun of defilement. Its oldest English sense is religious; the environmental sense is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pollution 经法语来自拉丁 pollutio，是一个表示「玷污」的名词。它最早的英语义项是宗教性的，环境义则是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: The verb behind the noun is usually divided into por- (a form of pro- 'forth') and luere 'to wash'. The deeper origin of luere is uncertain, and the relation sometimes drawn to lavare 'to wash' is a related-form hypothesis, not a proved descent.
items.cn: 这个名词背后的动词通常拆成 por-（pro-「向前」的一种形式）与 luere「洗」。luere 的更深来源不确定，有人把它与 lavare「洗」联系，那只是「相关形式」的假说，并非已证实的承继。

items.en: Polluere meant 'to defile, to corrupt'. How the washing element came to mean defiling is not fully explained; one account treats the prefix as intensive rather than directional.
items.cn: polluere 意为「弄脏、败坏」。「洗」的成分如何转为「弄脏」，并未得到完整解释；一种说法把前缀视为加强成分而非方向成分。

items.en: Late Latin pollutio named a defiling, especially ritual uncleanness, and this is the sense that entered English.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 pollutio 指玷污，尤指仪式上的不洁，进入英语的正是这一义项。

items.en: From the fourteenth century English pollution meant the desecration of sacred things or the state of being ritually unclean.
items.cn: 从十四世纪起，英语 pollution 指对神圣之物的亵渎或仪式上的不洁状态。

items.en: In the nineteenth century smoke, sewage and factory waste gave the word its modern environmental sense, and it soon became a public-health issue.
items.cn: 十九世纪，烟、污水与工厂废料赋予这个词现代环境义，它很快成为公共卫生议题。

items.en: Source uncertain (internal history of polluere, first date of the environmental sense): the semantic path from washing to defiling is unexplained and the first environmental citation is not fixed, so its date is approximate; any older form offered for luere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（polluere 的内部构造、环境义的首见年代）：从「洗」到「弄脏」的语义路径未获解释，环境义的最早书证也无定论，年代只能约计；凡为 luere 给出的更早形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same pollute stock that differ in grammar or role; group two holds other words for environmental damage, each naming a different part of the problem.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 pollute 词干、语法角色不同的形式；第二组是其他表示环境损害的词，各自命名问题的一个不同部分。

entries.definition: A single offending substance; pollution is the resulting condition or the whole accumulation.
entries.definitionCN: 一种肇事的物质；pollution 是造成的结果或整体累积。

entries.definition: To put harmful matter into a medium; the noun names what the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 把有害物质放入介质；名词指动词所产生的状态。

entries.definition: A person or firm that pollutes; it is a responsible party, not a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 造成污染的人或企业；它是责任方，而非状态。

entries.definition: A head, a vote survey or a hornless beast, from Middle English polle; the resemblance to pollute is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指头、投票调查或无角牲畜，出自中古英语 polle；与 pollute 的相似只是偶然。

entries.definition: The making impure of a substance or product; it need not harm an ecosystem, which pollution implies.
entries.definitionCN: 使物质或产品不纯；它未必危害生态，而 pollution 含有这一层。

entries.definition: A general lowering of quality or condition; pollution is one cause of environmental degradation.
entries.definitionCN: 品质或状况的普遍下降；污染是环境退化的一个原因。

entries.definition: The release of a substance into the air; pollution is the harm that follows from such releases.
entries.definitionCN: 物质向空气的排放；pollution 是这类排放带来的危害。

entries.definition: The clogging or dirtying of equipment, hulls or beds; it is a practical nuisance sense, not a public-health one.
entries.definitionCN: 设备、船体或床层的堵塞与污损；它是设备层面的麻烦义，而非公共卫生义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Pollution is the noun of pollute: the act of putting harm into a medium and the state that follows.
normal.cn: pollution 是 pollute 的名词：把危害放入介质的动作，以及随之而来的状态。

normal.en: The family runs pollute, pollutant, polluter, polluted and polluting.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pollute、pollutant、polluter、polluted 与 polluting。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the medium: air pollution, water pollution, soil pollution, noise pollution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出介质：空气污染、水污染、土壤污染、噪声污染。

normal.en: The oldest English sense was religious: pollution meant ritual uncleanness before it meant smoke.
normal.cn: 最早的英语义项是宗教性的：pollution 先指仪式上的不洁，后指烟尘。

normal.en: Poll looks alike but means 'head', so it is a false relative.
normal.cn: poll 形似而同源无关，意为「头」，是假同源。

abstract.en: Picture a clear river receiving one pipe and losing its colour downstream.
abstract.cn: 想象一条清河接入一根管子，下游就失了颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a night sky erased by a ring of lamps.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈路灯抹掉了夜空。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf filled with books that repeat nonsense.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上塞满反复讲胡话的书。

examples.en: Pollution in the estuary comes from farms far upstream.
examples.cn: 河口处的污染来自远在上游的农田。

examples.en: The city monitors pollution every hour at ten stations.
examples.cn: 该市在十个监测站每小时监测污染。

examples.en: Noise pollution from the highway reaches the school.
examples.cn: 公路的噪声污染传到了学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pollute（污染）+ ion」——把脏东西放进环境这件事，以及它造成的状态 → 污染

root: 拉丁 pollutio「玷污」< polluere「弄脏」；polluere 通常拆为 por-（pro- 变体）+ luere「洗」，但「洗」转为「弄脏」未获完整解释，luere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one intrusion: a clean medium is entered, its state changes, each medium gets its own name, energy and waste join the list, and the old religious image survives at one end while the metaphor of a spoiled shared medium survives at the other.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一次侵入展开：洁净介质被进入，状态改变，各介质各得一名，能量与废物加入清单，一端留着旧的宗教意象，另一端留着「共用介质被弄坏」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an oily sheen on a river bend, with reeds tangled in plastic cord.
core.cn: 核心意象：河湾上一层油光，芦苇缠着塑料绳。

branches.en: ACT AND STATE: English uses one noun for the putting-in and for what is left afterwards.
branches.cn: 动作与状态：英语用同一个名词兼指「放入」与「放入后剩下的」。

branches.en: THREE MEDIA: air, water and soil each make pollution visible in a different way.
branches.cn: 三种介质：空气、水与土壤各以不同方式让污染显形。

branches.en: ADDED ENERGY AND WASTE: noise, light and plastic all fit the same frame of something extra.
branches.cn: 能量与废物：噪声、光与塑料都落在「多出来的东西」这同一框架里。

branches.en: OLD ROOT: ritual defilement is the image from which the environmental sense grew.
branches.cn: 旧根：仪式上的玷污是环境义从中长出的意象。

branches.en: NEW ROOT: information pollution repeats the image in a shared medium of thought.
branches.cn: 新枝：信息污染在同一意象上重复，只是介质成了共用的思想空间。

intro.en: Pollution is a Latin noun of action with a debated root, so the suffix and prefix are clear while the semantic history of the root is not.
intro.cn: pollution 是拉丁动作名词，词根有争议，因此前缀与后缀清楚，而词根的语义历史不清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin polluere gives pollute, pollution, pollutant and polluter; -io, -ionis forms nouns of action in English -ion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 polluere 衍生 pollute、pollution、pollutant 与 polluter；-io, -ionis 在英语中构成 -ion 动作名词。

items.example: One account reads the prefix as directional.
items.exampleCN: 一种说法把这个前缀读作方向性的。

items.example: The washing element is the disputed half of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 「洗」这个成分是动词中有争议的一半。

items.example: Polluere named both ritual and physical uncleanness.
items.exampleCN: polluere 兼指仪式与物理上的不洁。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成动作名词。

items.meaning: a defiling; the state of being defiled

items.exampleCN: 受污染的小溪流着黑水。
造成污染的燃料被征税。

definition_zh: 池塘；鱼塘；养殖池；冷却池；大西洋（口语）
definition_en: a small area of still water, often made by people; also a managed basin for fish or for industrial water, and informally the Atlantic Ocean
core_image: 一圈土堤围住的一小片静水，水面映着低垂的柳枝
scene: 夏末的午后，村口的柳树把影子投在水面上，几只鸭子慢慢划过。Behind the mill, willow branches hung low over a quiet pond.
sceneCN: 这里的 pond 是「池塘」（第 1 个义项：小片静水）；句意为磨坊后面，柳枝低低地垂在一片安静的池塘上。图中可辨识物件：柳枝、水面、鸭子。

pos.zh: 池塘；鱼塘；养殖池；冷却池；大西洋（口语）

derivatives.zh: 由 pond 与 weed 复合而成，义为「池草；眼子菜类水草」
由 pond 与 side 复合而成，义为「池边的」
由 fish 与 pond 复合而成，义为「鱼塘」

senses.title: A small area of still water
senses.definition: a small area of still water, usually smaller than a lake and often dug or dammed by people
senses.definitionCN: 一片不大的静水，通常比湖小，多为人工挖成或筑堤蓄成
senses.example: Ducks floated quietly on the village pond.
senses.exampleCN: 鸭子静静地浮在村子的池塘上。
senses.why: The word began as a name for an enclosed place, and when the fence became an earth bank the same name settled on the water held inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指被围起来的地方；当围栏变成土堤，同一个名字就落到了被围在里面的水上。

senses.title: A basin kept for fish or waterfowl
senses.definition: a pond built or managed so that fish, ducks or other water animals can be raised in it
senses.definitionCN: 为养鱼、养鸭或其他水生动物而修建、管理的水体
senses.example: They dug three ponds behind the house for carp.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在屋后挖了三口鱼塘养鲤鱼。
senses.why: Once water could be held in one place, it could also be stocked, so the word widened from a patch of water to a working basin with a harvest.
senses.whyCN: 水一旦能被蓄在一处，就能往里放养生物，于是词义从一片水面扩展到有收成的生产水体。

senses.title: An engineered basin for a process
senses.definition: a basin built to hold water for cooling, settling or storing waste in an industrial process
senses.definitionCN: 工业生产中用来冷却、沉淀或存放废水的池子
senses.example: The plant pumps warm water into a cooling pond.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把温水抽进冷却池。
senses.why: Industry borrowed the word for any shallow basin that holds liquid, keeping the old shape of water shut in by a rim.
senses.whyCN: 工业借用了这个词来指任何盛液体的浅池，保留的仍是「水被边沿围住」这一古老形状。

senses.title: The Atlantic, in casual speech
senses.definition: the Atlantic Ocean, used informally by people on one side of it when speaking of the other side
senses.definitionCN: 大西洋的口语说法，岸这边的人用它来指对岸
senses.example: She moved across the pond twenty years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十年前搬到了大西洋对岸。
senses.why: Calling an ocean a pond is a deliberate understatement: two shores are treated as the banks of one small sheet of water, which makes the distance sound crossable.
senses.whyCN: 把大洋叫作池塘是故意的轻描淡写：两岸被当成一小片水的两个边，遥远的距离听起来就像能一步跨过。

intro.en: Pond first named a fenced place, then the water held behind a bank, and only later any small still water.
intro.cn: pond 最早指围起来的地方，随后指土堤拦住的水，最后才泛指任何小片静水。

items.en: The element pund- appears in pundfald, a pen for stray cattle, and meant an enclosed place rather than water.
items.cn: 古英语中的 pund- 见于 pundfald（关牲口的围栏），指的是被围起来的地方，与水无关。

items.en: Middle English ponde named an artificial body of water, typically a small lake held back by an earth bank.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ponde 指人工蓄起的水体，通常是被土堤拦住的小湖。

items.en: The enclosing fence of the old word was replaced by the bank of the pond, so the boundary stayed and the contents changed from animals to water.
items.cn: 旧词里围住场地的栅栏被池塘的土堤取代，边界还在，围住的东西却从牲口变成了水。

items.en: Modern English pond covers any small still water, whether dug for gardens, stocked with fish or built for a factory.
items.cn: 现代英语的 pond 泛指任何小片静水，无论是为花园挖的、养鱼的，还是给工厂建的。

items.en: The teasing phrase across the pond turns the Atlantic into a small sheet of water, and compounds such as cooling pond extend the word to industry.
items.cn: 玩笑说法 across the pond 把大西洋说成一小片水；cooling pond 这类复合词则把词义延伸到工业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short English words that differ from pond by a single letter; the near-meaning group gathers other names for still water.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pond 只差一两个字母的短词；近义组收其他表示静水的词。

entries.definition: A unit of weight or money, or an enclosure for animals; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 重量或货币单位，也指关动物的围栏；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Feeling affection or liking for someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 喜爱某人的；钟情的。

entries.definition: Something that ties people together, or a certificate of debt.
entries.definitionCN: 纽带；债券。

entries.definition: A sum of money kept for a special purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途保存的一笔钱；基金。

entries.definition: A lake or a small sheet of still water, now mostly used in literary writing and place names.
entries.definitionCN: 湖或小片静水，如今多见于文学描写与地名。

entries.definition: A small shallow patch of rainwater on the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 地面上由雨水积成的小浅水洼。

entries.definition: A large area of water surrounded by land.
entries.definitionCN: 被陆地环绕的大片水域；湖。

entries.definition: A large artificial lake used for storing water.
entries.definitionCN: 用于蓄水的大型人工湖；水库。

normalIntro.en: Pond is a word about a boundary: an enclosed place became an enclosed sheet of water, and the compounds show what people keep inside it.
normalIntro.cn: pond 是一个关于边界的词：被围住的地方变成了被围住的水面，而各类复合词则显示人们往里面放什么。

normal.en: Old English pundfald was a pen for cattle, so the earliest sense of the family is a fenced space, not a wet one.
normal.cn: 古英语 pundfald 是关牛的围栏，所以这一族词最早的意思是围起来的空间，而不是水。

normal.en: A pond is what you get when the fence around a place is replaced by a bank around water.
normal.cn: 当围住场地的栅栏换成围住水的土堤，得到的就是 pond。

normal.en: Fishpond and duck pond simply name the animals kept inside, which is the cheapest way to remember the word.
normal.cn: fishpond 与 duck pond 直接把养在里面的动物写出来，这是记住这个词最省力的办法。

normal.en: Pondweed grows where ponds are, so the compound -weed tells you the plant's home rather than its shape.
normal.cn: pondweed 长在池塘里，所以 -weed 这个复合成分告诉你的是植物的住处，而不是它的形状。

normal.en: Across the pond works because two coasts can be imagined as the two banks of one small stretch of water.
normal.cn: across the pond 之所以成立，是因为两岸可以被想象成一小片水的两个岸。

abstract.en: Every pond is a decision to stop water from moving on, which is why the word sits so close to dams and banks.
abstract.cn: 每个池塘都是「不让水继续流走」的决定，所以这个词总跟堤坝、岸沿挨在一起。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a fence now means a surface, a sign that boundaries outlive the things they were built for.
abstract.cn: 一个曾指栅栏的词如今指一片水面，说明边界往往比它当初围的东西活得更久。

abstract.en: Shrinking an ocean to a pond is language doing what maps cannot: making distance feel small enough to joke about.
abstract.cn: 把大洋缩成池塘，是语言做了地图做不到的事：让距离小到可以拿来开玩笑。

examples.en: The farm keeps a pond for ducks and carp.
examples.cn: 这个农场留了一口池塘养鸭子和鲤鱼。

examples.en: Willow branches brushed the surface of the pond.
examples.cn: 柳枝拂过池塘的水面。

examples.en: Her sister has lived across the pond for years.
examples.cn: 她姐姐在大西洋对岸住了很多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「胖得」——池塘里的鸭子吃得好，胖得游不动；记住 pond 是池塘。

root: 古英语 pund- 表示「围起来的地方」（见 pundfald「关牲口的围栏」），中古英语 ponde 转指被土堤围住的水，后来泛指小片静水；更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a small sheet of still water; the branches add what the water is kept for, and one loose figurative use turns the Atlantic into a pond.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一小片静水；各分支补出蓄水是为了什么，另有一处松散的比喻用法把大西洋说成池塘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low earth bank holding a small sheet of quiet water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道低低的土堤围住一小片安静的水。

branches.en: a duck gliding across a village pond at dusk
branches.cn: 黄昏时一只鸭子划过村口的池塘

branches.cn: 从鱼塘里提起滴水的渔网

branches.en: steam rising off a power station's cooling pond

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for pond; the word comes from an Old English element for an enclosure.
latinIntro.cn: pond 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它来自古英语中表示「围起来的地方」的成分。

senses.title: A small body of still water
senses.definition: a small area of still water, either left by rain or made by people
senses.definitionCN: 一小片不流动的水，或由雨水积成，或由人工砌成
senses.example: Rainwater collected in a shallow pool beside the road.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水在路边积成了一个浅浅的水洼。
senses.why: Old English pol named still water and the deep spots in a river, so the word starts from water that stays put instead of running on.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pol 指静水以及河中的深水处，所以这个词的起点是不往前流、留在原地的水。

senses.title: A basin built for swimming
senses.definition: an artificial basin filled with water and used for swimming
senses.definitionCN: 灌满水、供人游泳的人工水池
senses.example: The children swam in the hotel pool all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们整个下午都在旅馆的泳池里游泳。
senses.why: A pool is water held in one place, so a basin built to hold it for swimming needs no new word, only a purpose added in front.
senses.whyCN: pool 本来就是蓄在一处的水，因此供游泳的水池不必另造新词，只需在前面加一个用途。

senses.title: A shared supply of money or people
senses.definition: an amount of money, work or people contributed by many and used by all of them
senses.definitionCN: 由多方拿出、供大家共同使用的钱、工作或人力
senses.example: The company draws from a large pool of engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司从庞大的人才库中选用工程师。
senses.why: The game sense came from French poule, a common stake, and that shared pot of money gave English the idea of any supply that many people pay into and draw from.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自法语 poule（大家押下的赌注），那口公用的钱罐让英语引申出「众人凑入、众人取用」的资源。

senses.title: To gather things into one shared whole
senses.definition: to put money, effort or equipment together so that a group can use it
senses.definitionCN: 把钱、力气或设备合在一起，供一群人共同使用
senses.example: The two firms pooled their resources to finish the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司集中资源，才把这座桥修完。
senses.why: If a pool is a common pot, the verb is simply the act of filling it: each side drops something in before anyone draws anything out.
senses.whyCN: 如果 pool 是一口公用的罐子，动词就是往罐里放东西的动作：各方先各放一点，之后才谈取用。

senses.title: A table game played with cues
senses.definition: a game played on a cloth-covered table in which balls are struck with a long cue
senses.definitionCN: 在铺布球台上用长杆击球的游戏
senses.example: They spent the evening playing pool.
senses.exampleCN: 他们打了一晚上台球。
senses.why: In French poule the stakes were pooled before play, and the table game kept the name of that shared bet rather than any word for water.
senses.whyCN: 法语 poule 指开局前把赌注合在一起，这种球戏留下的是「公共赌注」的名字，与水毫无关系。

intro.en: Pool has two streams: an Old English word for still water, and a French word for a common stake that gave English the shared-fund and billiard senses.
intro.cn: pool 有两条来路：一条是古英语中表示静水的词，另一条是法语中表示公共赌注的词，后者带来「共用资金」与「台球」两个义项。

items.en: Old English pol meant a small body of water and could also name a deep, slow spot in a river.
items.cn: 古英语的 pol 指一小片水，也可指河中水深流缓的地方。

items.en: Related forms appear in Middle Dutch poel and Old High German pfuol, but the earlier origin of the set is uncertain.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 poel 与古高地德语 pfuol 有相关形式，但这组词更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Middle English pool broadened to ponds, mill dams and any still water, natural or dug.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pool 扩展到池塘、磨坊水坝以及任何静水，无论天然还是人工。

items.en: French poule, literally a hen, named the stakes that card players put into one pot, and English borrowed the word for that common fund.
items.cn: 法语 poule 本义是母鸡，用来指牌戏玩家押进同一口罐子的赌注，英语借来表示这笔公共的钱。

items.en: From card tables the shared-fund sense spread to typing pools and car pools, while the cue game kept the name of the pooled stakes.
items.cn: 从牌桌出发，「公共资金」义扩展到打字员组、拼车等说法，而用球杆玩的游戏则留下了「公共赌注」这个名字。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers one-syllable words that differ from pool by a letter; the near-meaning group gathers other containers and bodies of water.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pool 只差一个字母的单音节词；近义组收其他盛水之处与水体。

normalIntro.en: Pool joins two old ideas, still water and a common stake, and almost every sense can be reached from one of them.
normalIntro.cn: pool 把两个古老的意思合在一起：静水与公共赌注；几乎每个义项都能从其中之一走到。

normal.en: Old English pol meant still water and a deep spot in a river, which is why the water senses need no explanation.
normal.cn: 古英语 pol 指静水与河中的深水处，所以与水有关的义项不需要额外解释。

normal.en: French poule literally means hen; it named the stakes players pushed into one pot, and that pot became the shared fund.
normal.cn: 法语 poule 本义是母鸡，指玩家押进同一口罐子的赌注，这口罐子后来成了共用资金。

normal.en: A talent pool and a gene pool both use the image of a common supply that people or traits are drawn from.
normal.cn: talent pool 与 gene pool 用的都是「公共储备」这个意象，人或性状从中取用。

normal.en: Pool resources is the verb built from the pot: put in first, take out later, and the group gains what no one had alone.
normal.cn: pool resources 是从那口罐子来的动词：先放进去，后面再取，群体便得到了单个人没有的东西。

normal.en: Pool table keeps the gambling name, not the water name, which is why billiards has nothing to do with swimming.
normal.cn: pool table 保留的是赌博的名字，不是水的名字，所以台球与游泳无关。

abstract.en: Water that stops moving and money that stops circulating in private hands follow the same shape: something gathered into one place.
abstract.cn: 停止流动的水，与不再留在私人手里的钱，形状相同：都是被聚到一处的东西。

abstract.en: A pool is a promise that what is put in will be shared out, whether it holds water, money or engineers.
abstract.cn: pool 是一种承诺：放进去的东西会被分用，无论里面装的是水、钱还是工程师。

abstract.en: Two unrelated histories meeting in one spelling is a reminder that a word can carry more than one memory.
abstract.cn: 两段毫不相干的历史挤进同一个拼写，提醒人一个词可以同时带着不止一段记忆。

examples.en: Rainwater collected in a shallow pool beside the road.

definition_zh: 贫穷的；穷困的；差的；低劣的；可怜的；贫瘠的；缺乏……的
definition_en: having very little money, of low quality, deserving pity, or lacking something that is needed
core_image: 一件短了一截的旧外套，袖口磨得发白，衣袋里空空如也
scene: 冬天的清晨，屋里没有暖气，孩子的外套短了一截，袖口磨得发白。The family was too poor to buy coal that winter.
sceneCN: 这里的 poor 是「贫穷的」（第 1 个义项：缺钱）；句意为那个冬天这家人穷得买不起煤。图中可辨识物件：短了一截的外套、磨白的袖口、没有暖气的屋子。

pos.zh: 贫穷的；穷困的；差的；低劣的；可怜的；贫瘠的；缺乏……的

derivatives.zh: 由 poor 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「很差地；不力地」；作形容词时指「身体不适的」
与 poor 同出拉丁语 pauper，经古法语 poverte 而来，义为「贫困；匮乏」
由 poor 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「贫穷；低劣」

senses.title: Having very little money
senses.definition: having so little money that ordinary needs such as food, heat or clothing are hard to meet
senses.definitionCN: 钱少到难以应付吃饭、取暖、穿衣这类日常需要
senses.example: The family was too poor to heat the house.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人穷得连房子都供不起暖气。
senses.why: Latin pauper described a person of small means, and the word came into English through French carrying that plain material sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pauper 形容家底微薄的人，这个词经法语进入英语时，带的就是这层朴素的物质含义。

senses.title: Of low quality
senses.definition: not as good as it should be in strength, sound, finish or standard
senses.definitionCN: 在结实、清晰、做工或水准上达不到应有的程度
senses.example: The recording was poor and hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 录音效果很差，听不太清楚。
senses.why: A person can be poor in money, so a thing can be poor in what it ought to have; the same measure of lack is applied to quality.
senses.whyCN: 人可以穷在钱上，东西也可以穷在它本该有的地方；判断质量用的仍是同一把「缺」的尺子。

senses.title: Deserving pity
senses.definition: unfortunate enough to make other people feel sorry for them
senses.definitionCN: 处境不幸，使别人替其难过
senses.example: The poor dog waited in the rain for its owner.
senses.exampleCN: 那只可怜的狗在雨里等着主人。
senses.why: Someone who has too little is exposed to harm, so the word slides from naming the lack to naming the feeling that lack stirs in others.
senses.whyCN: 拥有的太少就容易受伤害，于是这个词从指「缺」滑向指「缺」在旁人心里激起的怜惜。

senses.title: Lacking a needed substance
senses.definition: containing too little of something that plants or bodies need, as in poor soil or water poor in minerals
senses.definitionCN: 所含的植物或身体所需之物太少，如贫瘠的土壤、缺少矿物质的水
senses.example: This soil is too poor for wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 这土太贫瘠，种不了小麦。
senses.why: The oldest frame survives in phrases such as poor in iron, where the word simply marks what a thing does not have enough of.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的结构留在 poor in iron 这类说法里，那里的 poor 只是标出一件东西哪一样不够。

intro.en: Poor comes from Latin pauper through Old French, and the whole family keeps the idea of having or producing too little.
intro.cn: poor 经古法语来自拉丁语 pauper，整族词都保留着「拥有或产出太少」的意思。

items.en: Pauper meant poor or of small means, and it could even describe soil that yields little.
items.cn: pauper 意为贫穷的、家底薄的，甚至能形容产出很少的土地。

items.en: The noun paupertas named poverty and want, and it is the source of the English word poverty.
items.cn: 名词 paupertas 指贫困与匮乏，是英语 poverty 的来源。

items.en: Old French povre kept both the material sense and a stronger tone of wretchedness and misfortune.
items.cn: 古法语的 povre 既保留物质上的贫穷，也带有更重的凄惨与不幸意味。

items.en: Middle English spellings such as povre and poure competed, and the form with -ou- became the standard poor.
items.cn: 中古英语的 povre、poure 等拼写并行，带 -ou- 的形式最终成为标准拼写 poor。

items.en: Modern English extended the word from money to quality, health, soil and finally to a tone of pity.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义从钱财扩展到质量、健康、土壤，最后还带上了一层怜悯的语气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the Latin stem or the sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for having little, being bad or deserving pity.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁词干或读音相近的词；近义组收表示「贫穷」「差」「可怜」的词。

normalIntro.en: Poor is a Latin word for small means, and its family shows how a judgement about money becomes a judgement about quality and then a feeling of pity.
normalIntro.cn: poor 是拉丁语中表示「家底薄」的词，它这一族显示了关于钱的判断如何变成关于质量的判断，再变成怜悯。

normal.en: Pauper is the Latin word itself used as an English noun: a pauper is a person who is poor.
normal.cn: pauper 就是那个拉丁词直接当英语名词用：a pauper 就是穷人。

normal.en: Poverty comes from Latin paupertas, the noun built beside pauper, so the two words are cousins rather than parent and child.
normal.cn: poverty 来自拉丁语 paupertas，是与 pauper 并列造出的名词，所以两者是表亲，而不是父子。

normal.en: Old French povre lost its ending on the way into English, leaving the short form poor.
normal.cn: 古法语的 povre 在进入英语的路上丢掉了词尾，留下短短的 poor。

normal.en: Poor quality and poor health both keep the original idea of lacking what should be there.
normal.cn: poor quality 与 poor health 都保留了原来的意思：缺了本该有的东西。

normal.en: The poor is an adjective standing in for a noun, so it takes a plural verb: the poor are, not the poor is.
normal.cn: the poor 是形容词顶替名词，所以配复数动词：说 the poor are，不说 the poor is。

abstract.en: A word for having too little turns into a word for being bad, which shows how easily a judgement about means becomes a judgement about worth.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「拥有太少」的词变成了表示「不好」的词，说明对家底的判断多容易变成对价值的判断。

abstract.en: Calling a dog poor does not measure its money; it measures the gap between what it has and what it needs.
abstract.cn: 把一只狗叫作 poor，量的不是它的钱，而是它拥有的与它需要的之间的差距。

abstract.en: Poor soil and a poor excuse share one grammar: something is missing that the situation requires.
abstract.cn: 贫瘠的土壤与蹩脚的借口共用一个语法：这情形需要的东西缺了。

examples.en: The family was too poor to heat the house.
examples.cn: 这家人穷得连房子都供不起暖气。

examples.en: The recording was poor and hard to follow.
examples.cn: 录音效果很差，听不太清楚。

examples.en: This soil is too poor for wheat.
examples.cn: 这土太贫瘠，种不了小麦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破」——穷得衣服都破了；记住 poor 是贫穷的。

root: 经古法语 povre 来自拉丁语 pauper（贫穷的、少产的）；pauper 的更早来源不确定，一般认为与「产出少」有关。同族词有 poverty、pauper。

sensesIntro.en: The core is having too little; the branches apply that lack to money, to quality, to the feeling of pity, and to soil or water short of a substance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「拥有的太少」；各分支把这种「缺」分别用到钱财、质量、怜悯之情，以及缺某种成分的土壤或水。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty pocket and a coat whose sleeves have worn thin.
core.cn: 核心意象：空空的口袋，和袖口磨得又薄又短的外套。

branches.en: a cold room where the heating has been switched off
branches.cn: 暖气关掉的冷屋子

branches.en: a crackling recording that swallows the speaker's words
branches.cn: 吞掉说话人字句的沙沙录音

branches.en: a wet dog waiting by a gate for its owner
branches.cn: 在门口雨里等主人的湿狗

branches.en: a field where wheat will not grow
branches.cn: 长不出小麦的一块地

branches.cn: 同一种「缺」，一次被判为质量差，一次被判为不幸

intro.cn: 这个词由表示家底薄的拉丁形容词及其名词、动词承载，再加上两个英语后缀，构成副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: popular music as a genre; a short sharp bursting sound; to burst or open with such a sound; and to appear or go somewhere suddenly
core_image: 手臂边一只气球突然炸开，碎片飞出去，屋里的人全都抬头
scene: 街角的小店门口挂着旧音箱，午后的阳光斜进来，一群学生跟着旋律点头。The radio kept playing one pop song after another while the students waited for the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 pop 指「流行音乐」（第 1 个义项：旋律好记、面向大众的音乐）；句意为学生们等公交时，收音机一首接一首地放着流行歌。图中可辨识物件：旧音箱、斜照进来的阳光、等车的学生。

pos.zh: 流行音乐；砰的一声
爆开；突然冒出；匆匆去一趟
流行音乐的；通俗的

derivatives.zh: 由 pop 与 corn 复合而成，取「受热爆开」的旧义，义为「爆米花」
由 pop 加表示工具或人的 -er 构成，义为「爆米花锅；按扣」
由 pop 加 -ing 构成，义为「连续的爆响；机械舞」

senses.title: Popular music as a genre
senses.definition: a style of music with a strong beat and easily remembered tunes, made for a wide audience rather than for specialists
senses.definitionCN: 节奏鲜明、旋律好记，面向广大听众而非专业圈子的音乐类型
senses.example: She sang along to every pop song on the radio.
senses.exampleCN: 收音机里每一首流行歌她都跟着唱。
senses.why: This sense is a mid-twentieth-century clipping of popular, taken from phrases such as popular music, so the name says who the music is made for rather than how it is composed.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是二十世纪中叶从 popular 截短来的，取的是 popular music 一类说法，所以名字说的是音乐做给谁听，而不是它怎么写。

senses.title: A short sharp bursting sound
senses.definition: a small explosive noise made when something bursts, snaps or is struck
senses.definitionCN: 东西爆开、绷断或被击中时发出的短促爆响
senses.example: The paper bag gave a loud pop when she hit it.
senses.exampleCN: 她一巴掌拍下去，纸袋砰地响了一声。
senses.why: This sense is generally taken to be imitative: the word copies the noise of a small burst, which is why one form can name both the sound and the event behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项一般认为来自拟声：词本身在模仿小东西爆开的声响，所以同一种形式既能指声音，也能指发出声音的那件事。

senses.title: To burst or open with a sharp sound
senses.definition: to burst, open or come out suddenly with a small sharp noise
senses.definitionCN: 伴随着短促响声突然爆开、弹开或冒出来
senses.example: The cork popped out of the bottle and hit the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶塞砰地从瓶口弹出来，撞到了天花板上。
senses.why: Once the sound-word had named the noise of bursting, English could turn it into a verb for whatever produced that noise, and a cork leaving a bottle is the clearest case.
senses.whyCN: 拟声词一旦指认了爆裂的响声，英语就能把它变成动词，指发出这声响的东西；瓶塞飞出瓶口就是最清楚的例子。

senses.title: To appear or go somewhere suddenly
senses.definition: to come into view suddenly and briefly, or to go somewhere quickly for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 突然而短暂地出现在眼前，或很快地去某处一趟
senses.example: A rabbit popped out of the hole and froze.
senses.exampleCN: 一只兔子突然从洞里冒出来，随即定住不动。
senses.why: A burst is sudden and over in a moment; English carries that suddenness over to anything that appears or leaves in a flash, which is how the verb reaches rabbits and short errands.
senses.whyCN: 爆开是一下子发生、一下就结束的；英语把这种突然挪到任何一闪而现或一闪而去的事情上，动词于是能用来说兔子，也能说匆匆跑一趟。

intro.en: English has two words written pop: an imitative syllable for a bang, and a twentieth-century clipping of popular. The spellings merged, the histories did not.
intro.cn: 英语里有两个拼作 pop 的词：一个模仿爆响，一个是二十世纪对 popular 的截短。拼写合流了，来历并没有合流。

items.en: Populus named the people as a body, the crowd whose taste decides what becomes common.
items.cn: populus 指作为整体的民众，也就是他们的喜好决定了什么东西会变得普遍。

items.en: Popularis meant belonging to or pleasing the people, and it is the adjective that pop would later shorten.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的、讨民众喜欢的，正是后来被 pop 截短的那个形容词。

items.en: Generally regarded as imitative, the short word for a small explosion copies the sound itself and has no connection with Latin.
items.cn: 一般认为表示小爆炸的 pop 是拟声词，直接模仿声音，与拉丁语没有关系。

items.en: In the mid-twentieth century popular music was clipped to pop, used first as a modifier and soon as a noun in its own right.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶，popular music 被截短成 pop，先作修饰语，很快又独立作名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps both strands: a bang, a quick errand and a whole shelf of music, all spelled the same way.
items.cn: 现代英语两条线都留着：一声爆响、一趟快去快回、一整排音乐，拼写完全一样。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the populus family behind the music sense; the near-meaning group collects other words for popular music and for sudden movement.
note.cn: 形近组顺着音乐义背后的 populus 词族展开；近义组收表示流行音乐与突然动作的其他词。

entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的；pop 正是它的截短形式。

entries.definition: The state of being liked or accepted by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱或接受的状况。

entries.definition: To make something widely known or liked.

entries.definitionCN: 非常成功的歌曲或唱片；热门歌曲。

entries.definition: The music, taste or opinion accepted by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 被大多数人接受的音乐、品味或观点；主流。

normalIntro.en: The word carries two histories at once: a copied sound and a shortened adjective, and most of its uses can be traced to one or the other.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时背着两段来历：一个模仿来的声音，一个被截短的形容词；它的用法大多能归到其中一条。

normal.en: Popular music was shortened to pop, so a pop song is simply a song meant for everybody.
normal.cn: popular music 被缩成 pop，所以 pop song 就是给所有人听的歌。

normal.en: The bang is imitative: say the word sharply and you have already made the sound.
normal.cn: 爆响那个义项是拟声的：把这个词短促地念出来，声音就已经发出来了。

normal.en: Pop up keeps the idea of a burst: something appears as if it had just exploded into view.
normal.cn: pop up 保留了「突然爆开」的意思：某物像是刚炸出来一样出现在眼前。

normal.en: Pop into a shop applies the same suddenness to a short errand, in and out in a moment.
normal.cn: pop into a shop 把同一种突然用在短程跑腿上，进去又出来，只用一会儿。

normal.en: Popcorn is named for the moment the kernel bursts, so the compound preserves the oldest sense.
normal.cn: popcorn 得名于玉米粒爆开的那一刻，这个复合词保存了最古老的义项。

abstract.en: One syllable carries both a drum hit and a hit song: noise and culture share a spelling.
abstract.cn: 一个音节既装着鼓点的一击，也装着一首热门歌：声音和文化共用一种拼写。

abstract.en: A balloon, a cork, a rabbit: the same snap marks every sudden appearance.
abstract.cn: 气球、瓶塞、兔子：同一声脆响标记着每一次突然出现。

abstract.en: Pop is what a crowd makes common, so the word for the people sits silently inside it.
abstract.cn: pop 指人群使之变得普遍的东西，所以表示民众的那个词静静藏在它里面。

examples.en: The children danced to a pop song in the kitchen.
examples.cn: 孩子们在厨房里跟着一首流行歌跳舞。

examples.en: The balloon popped and the dog ran off.
examples.cn: 气球砰地爆了，狗跑开了。

examples.en: A message popped up on the screen.
examples.cn: 屏幕上突然弹出一条消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡泡」——泡泡一破就是砰的一声；pop 又是人人会哼的流行歌。

root: 一般认为有两个来源：表示爆响的 pop 是拟声词；表示流行音乐的 pop 是 popular 的截短形式，而 popular 出自拉丁语 populus（民众）。

sensesIntro.en: Two origins feed one spelling: the sharp sound and its suddenness on one side, mass-market music on the other.
sensesIntro.cn: 两种来历汇成一个拼写：一边是爆响与随之而来的突然，另一边是面向大众的音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon bursting at arm's length, its skin flying off while everyone looks up.
core.cn: 核心意象：手臂边上一只气球突然炸开，碎片飞出去，所有人都抬头看。

branches.cn: 有人冲进小店买牛奶

branches.en: one short word for a bang and for a hit tune
branches.cn: 一个短词同时指爆响和热门曲子

intro.en: The word rests on two layers: an imitative English syllable, and the Latin family of populus. In that family -ar builds the adjective popular, -ity builds the noun of state, and -ize builds the verb of making; pop itself is only a clipping of the -ar form.
intro.cn: 这个词压着两层东西：一个拟声的英语音节，以及拉丁语 populus 词族。在这个词族里，-ar 造形容词 popular，-ity 造表状态的名词，-ize 造表「使……」的动词；pop 本身只是那个 -ar 形容词的截短。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 受欢迎的；大众的；通俗的；民众的；普遍的
definition_en: liked or approved by many people; made for ordinary people rather than specialists; of the people as a political source; and held by most people
core_image: 小店门口排起长队，路过的人不知道卖什么，也先跟着排上
scene: 放学后的面馆门口总有人排队，队伍拐过墙角，连附近上班的人也来凑热闹。That noodle shop is popular with students because it is cheap and fast.
sceneCN: 这里 popular 指「受欢迎的」（第 1 个义项：被很多人喜欢）；句意为这家面馆便宜又上得快，很受学生欢迎。图中可辨识场景：排到墙角的长队、放学的学生、探头张望的路人。

pos.zh: 受欢迎的；大众的；通俗的；民众的；普遍的

由 popular 加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地；由民众」
由 popular 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不受欢迎的」

senses.title: Liked by many people
senses.definition: liked, approved of or supported by a large number of people
senses.definitionCN: 被很多人喜欢、认可或支持的
senses.example: The new teacher quickly became popular with her class.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的老师很快就受到班上学生的欢迎。
senses.why: Latin popularis meant belonging to the people; a thing that belongs to everybody is one everybody is ready to accept, so approval grows out of that shared ownership.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 popularis 意为属于民众的；一样东西既然属于所有人，大家就都愿意接受它，「受欢迎」正是从这种共有关系里长出来的。

senses.title: Made for ordinary people
senses.definition: designed for ordinary people rather than for experts, and therefore easy to follow
senses.definitionCN: 面向普通人而非专家，因而容易听懂的
senses.example: He writes popular books about astronomy for readers with no training.
senses.exampleCN: 他写的天文读物面向没有受过专业训练的读者。
senses.why: If something is of the people, it is also for the people, so the word came to mark work that avoids the language of specialists.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西属于民众，自然也是做给民众的，于是这个词用来标记那些避开专家术语的作品。

senses.title: Of the people as a political source
senses.definition: relating to ordinary citizens, especially as the source of political authority
senses.definitionCN: 与普通公民有关的，尤指权力来自他们的
senses.example: The constitution was approved by a popular vote.
senses.exampleCN: 这部宪法经民众投票获得通过。
senses.why: The oldest political sense keeps the Latin meaning almost untouched: authority rests with populus, the people, not with a ruler above them.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的政治义几乎原封不动保留了拉丁含义：权力属于 populus（民众），而不是属于高居于他们之上的统治者。

senses.title: Held by most people
senses.definition: believed or repeated by a large part of the public, whether or not it is true
senses.definitionCN: 被大部分公众相信或传说的，不论真假
senses.example: It is a popular belief that we only use ten percent of our brains.
senses.exampleCN: 人们普遍相信我们只用了大脑的百分之十。
senses.why: Once an idea belongs to the many, it counts as popular even when it is wrong, which is why the word can sit directly beside belief and misconception.
senses.whyCN: 一个说法一旦属于很多人，即使它是错的也被称作 popular，所以这个词能直接修饰「看法」和「误解」。

intro.en: Popular came from Latin through French with the plain sense of belonging to the people; only later did English add the warmer sense of being liked.
intro.cn: popular 经法语来自拉丁语，本义只是「属于民众的」；「受喜爱」这层更暖的意思是很晚才由英语添上的。

items.en: Populus was the body of citizens, the people seen as a single crowd.
items.cn: populus 指公民的整体，是把人们看作一群人。

items.en: Popularis meant belonging to, pleasing or favouring the people, and it could describe a politician who courted them.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的、讨民众喜欢的、站在民众一边的，也能形容讨好民众的政治人物。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as populaire, keeping both the neutral and the approving tones.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 populaire，中性义与赞许义都保留着。

items.en: Middle English populere meant common, of the common people, and could still carry a hint of vulgar.
items.cn: 中古英语的 populere 意为普通的、平民的，仍可能带一点「粗俗」的意味。

items.en: Modern English pushed the word towards approval and, in politics, towards the people as the source of authority.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义推向「受认可」，在政治语境里则推向「权力来自民众」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the populus family and its negated form; the near-meaning group gathers words for being widely known or widely held.
note.cn: 形近组收 populus 词族及其否定形式；近义组收表示广为人知、广为接受的词。

entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的状态或程度。

entries.definition: To make something widely known, used or liked.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知、广为使用或广受欢迎。

entries.definition: Full of people; having a large population.
entries.definitionCN: 人口众多的；人烟稠密的。

entries.definition: Not liked or approved of by most people.

entries.definition: Known by a great many people.
entries.definitionCN: 被很多人知道的；著名的。

entries.definition: Found, done or believed by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 大多数人都有的、做的或相信的；常见的。

entries.definition: Existing or happening over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大范围或许多人中存在的；普遍的。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with a Latin noun for the people, and each modern sense measures some way in which a thing belongs to them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起于拉丁语里表示民众的名词，每个现代义项都在衡量某样东西以何种方式属于他们。

normal.en: Latin popularis meant of the people, and being liked is simply being accepted by the people who own it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 popularis 意为属于民众的，而「被喜欢」不过是被拥有它的那群人接受。

normal.en: Popular and population share populus: one counts approval, the other counts heads.
normal.cn: popular 与 population 共用 populus：一个数的是认可，一个数的是人头。

normal.en: Popularity is popular plus -ity, the state of being liked seen as a quantity.
normal.cn: popularity 是 popular 加 -ity，把「被喜欢」看成一种可计量的状态。

normal.en: Popularize is popular plus -ize, to make something common among people.
normal.cn: popularize 是 popular 加 -ize，让某样东西在人们中间变得普遍。

normal.en: Popular with names the crowd that likes it; popular for names the reason.
normal.cn: popular with 后面接喜欢它的人群；popular for 后面接喜欢它的原因。

abstract.en: A queue outside a small shop is popularity made visible.
abstract.cn: 小店门口的一条长队，就是看得见的人气。

abstract.en: What belongs to everyone ends up pleasing everyone, so ownership turns into affection.
abstract.cn: 属于所有人的东西，最后会让所有人喜欢，所有权就这样变成了好感。

abstract.en: A word can be popular and still be wrong, which is why belief takes the same adjective as music.
abstract.cn: 一个说法可以很流行又完全是错的，所以「看法」和音乐共用同一个形容词。

examples.en: This song is popular with children.
examples.cn: 这首歌很受孩子们欢迎。

examples.en: Popular science books explain hard ideas in plain words.
examples.cn: 科普读物用平实的语言解释难懂的概念。

examples.en: The mayor was elected by popular vote.
examples.cn: 市长是通过民众投票选出的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡普乐」——把知识泡进普通人的快乐里，大家就都喜欢；popular 就是受欢迎的、大众的。

root: 拉丁语 populus（民众）→ popularis（属于民众的）→ 古法语 populaire → 英语 popular；同族还有 population、populace。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is belonging to the people; it then splits into being liked, being made for them, coming from them politically, and being believed by them.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「属于民众」；由此分出被他们喜欢、为他们而做、政治上来自他们，以及被他们相信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue curling round the corner of a small shop, strangers joining it without asking why.
core.cn: 核心意象：小店门口的长队拐过墙角，陌生人没问缘由也排了进去。

branches.en: a queue curling round the corner of a noodle shop
branches.cn: 绕着面馆墙角的长队

branches.en: a plain-language guide to the stars on a bestseller table
branches.cn: 畅销书台上那本讲星星的通俗读物

branches.en: a ballot box where each citizen counts once
branches.cn: 每位公民都只算一票的投票箱

branches.en: a saying repeated in every kitchen and every office
branches.cn: 每个厨房和办公室都在重复的一句老话

branches.en: a leader who is both liked and chosen
branches.cn: 既被喜欢又被选出来的领导人

intro.en: A Latin noun for the people and its adjective carry the word, and the English suffixes divide the labour: -ar makes the adjective, -ity the noun of state, -ize the verb of making.
intro.cn: 一个表示民众的拉丁名词及其形容词撑起这个词，英语后缀则各管一段：-ar 造形容词，-ity 造表状态的名词，-ize 造表「使……」的动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 人口；全体居民；种群；（统计）总体
definition_en: the people living in a place, or any group of individuals counted together, including a breeding group of animals or a complete set of data
core_image: 一张城市鸟瞰图，屋顶密密麻麻，每个小点代表一个人，远处还有一片标着虫鸟的林子
scene: 这座小城的人口在二十年间翻了一倍，供水却始终没跟上。The city's population doubled in twenty years, and the water supply never caught up.
sceneCN: 这里 population 是「人口、居民总数」（第 1 个义项：某地居民的整体数量）；句意：这座城市的人口在二十年间翻了一番，供水却始终没跟上。图中可辨识物件：密集屋顶、代表居民的小点、远处的林地与鸟群；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 人口；全体居民；种群；总体
