senses.title: Optimistic and hopeful
senses.titleCN: 积极的：朝好处看的那种劲头
senses.definition: expecting good things and focusing on what can go well
senses.definitionCN: 期待好事、把注意力放在能顺利之处
senses.example: She stayed positive even after the third rejection.
senses.exampleCN: 即使被拒三次，她仍然保持积极。
senses.why: The word's core is 'laid down, definite'. A positive mind is one that has settled on the good outcome rather than leaving it open.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是“被确定下来”。积极的心态，就是把结果定在好处上，而不是让它悬着。

senses.title: Expressing agreement or yes
senses.definition: expressing agreement, approval, or an affirmative answer
senses.definitionCN: 表达同意、赞许或肯定回答
senses.example: We received a positive reply within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 我们一天之内就收到了肯定的答复。
senses.why: A positive answer is one that has been fixed: not maybe, not pending, but settled in the affirmative.
senses.whyCN: 肯定的回答是被固定下来的回答：不是也许，不是待定，而是定在“是”这一边。

senses.title: Good or beneficial in effect
senses.titleCN: 正面的：带来好结果的那一面
senses.definition: producing a good or useful effect
senses.definitionCN: 产生良好或有用的效果
senses.example: The new bus route had a positive impact on local shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新公交线路对本地商铺产生了正面影响。
senses.why: What is settled and real tends to be counted on the good side. Positive becomes the label for effects we want more of.
senses.whyCN: 被确定、被落实的东西往往被算在好的一边。positive 成了“我们希望更多”的效果的标签。

senses.title: Definite and undeniable
senses.titleCN: 确凿的：摆在那里，不容否认
senses.definition: clear, definite, and not open to doubt
senses.definitionCN: 清楚、确定、不容怀疑
senses.example: We have positive proof that the letter was forged.
senses.exampleCN: 我们有确凿证据证明这封信是伪造的。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: in law, positive meant formally laid down. What is laid down is not a matter of opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：在法律上，positive 指正式规定下来的。被规定下来的，就不是意见问题。

senses.title: Medical: showing the condition is present
senses.titleCN: 阳性的：查出了那个东西
senses.definition: showing that a particular substance, infection, or condition is present in a test
senses.definitionCN: 表示在检测中发现某种物质、感染或状况确实存在
senses.example: He tested positive for the virus but had no symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 他的病毒检测呈阳性，但没有症状。
senses.why: A test is a yes-or-no question put to the body. Positive means the thing asked about is definitely there, not absent.
senses.whyCN: 检测是向身体提出的一个是非题。positive 表示所问之物确实存在，而非缺席。

senses.title: Mathematics: above zero
senses.definition: of a number, greater than zero
senses.definitionCN: 指数值大于零
senses.example: Multiplying two negative numbers gives a positive result.
senses.exampleCN: 两个负数相乘得到正数结果。
senses.why: On a number line, positive marks the direction that counts upward from zero. The sign is a settled direction.
senses.whyCN: 在数轴上，正号标记从零点向上计数的方向。这个符号是一个确定下来的方向。

senses.title: Physics: carrying positive charge
senses.titleCN: 正电的：与电子相反的那种电荷
senses.definition: having the kind of electric charge carried by protons, opposite to that of electrons
senses.definitionCN: 带有质子所携的那种电荷，与电子所带电荷相反
senses.example: The positive terminal is marked with a plus sign.
senses.exampleCN: 正极用加号标出。
senses.why: Franklin's convention named one kind of charge positive, and the label stuck. It is a naming decision, not a claim about which charge is better.
senses.whyCN: 富兰克林的约定把其中一种电荷命名为 positive，这个叫法沿用至今。它是命名决定，并不表示哪种电荷“更好”。

senses.title: Grammar: the base degree
senses.definition: in grammar, the simple form of an adjective or adverb, before comparison
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指形容词或副词未作比较的简单形式
senses.example: Good is the positive degree; better and best are the comparative and superlative.
senses.exampleCN: good 是原级；better 与 best 分别是比较级和最高级。
senses.why: The base form states a quality outright, with nothing added. It is the form laid down before any comparison modifies it.
senses.whyCN: 原级直接陈述一种性质，不加任何东西。它是任何比较来改动之前就已定下的形式。

intro.en: Positive comes from a Latin adjective meaning 'settled by agreement'. Its history runs from law to logic to mathematics to electricity, and only recently to optimism.
intro.cn: positive 来自一个意为“经约定确定下来”的拉丁形容词。它的历史从法律走到逻辑、数学、电学，而“乐观”这一义其实很晚才出现。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to put, place'. Its past participle positus, 'placed, set down', is the stem of the whole family: position, deposit, compose, positive.
items.cn: ponere 意为“放置”。其过去分词 positus“被放置的、被定下的”，是整个词族的词干：position、deposit、compose、positive。

items.en: Positivus meant 'settled by agreement, conventional'. In medieval law it described rules laid down by authority, as opposed to natural law.
items.cn: positivus 意为“经约定确定的、约定俗成的”。在中世纪法律中，它指由权威制定下来的规则，与自然法相对。

items.en: English positive appears in the 14th century first in legal and philosophical writing, with the sense 'formally laid down, absolute'.
items.cn: 英语 positive 于 14 世纪出现，最早见于法律与哲学写作，意为“正式规定的、绝对的”。

items.en: By the 15th and 16th centuries it means 'definite, not open to doubt', and it also enters grammar for the uncompared degree of an adjective.
items.cn: 到 15、16 世纪，它表示“确定的、不容怀疑”，并进入语法，指形容词未作比较的原级。

items.en: From the 18th century the word labels the direction above zero and, after Franklin, the kind of electric charge called positive. Photography later adds the positive image.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，这个词标记零点以上的方向；在富兰克林之后，又标记被称为正的那种电荷。摄影随后又加上“正片”。

items.en: The everyday sense 'hopeful, optimistic' is a 20th-century development. It is the newest layer and is not found in the older legal or scientific uses.
items.cn: “充满希望、乐观”的日常义是 20 世纪的产物。它是最新的一层，在较早的法律或科学用法中找不到。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin participle. The second group collects words for approval, certainty, and good effect.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个拉丁分词上。第二组收表示赞同、确定与良好效果的词。

entries.definition: in a positive way, or absolutely. It also serves as an intensifier: positively dangerous means definitely dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 以积极的方式，或绝对地。它也用作强调词：positively dangerous 意为“绝对危险”。

entries.definition: to suggest or assume something as a fact. It comes from Latin positus, the same participle behind positive.
entries.definitionCN: 提出或假定某事为事实。它来自拉丁 positus，即 positive 背后的同一个分词。

entries.definition: a place or a point of view. From positio, a noun built on the same participle positus.
entries.definitionCN: 位置或观点。来自 positio，由同一个分词 positus 构成的名词。

entries.definition: the antiparticle of the electron, with positive charge. Formed in the 1930s from positive plus electron.
entries.definitionCN: 电子的反粒子，带正电。20 世纪 30 年代由 positive 与 electron 拼合而成。

entries.definition: expecting good outcomes. Optimistic is narrower than positive, which also covers agreement, proof, and electric charge.
entries.definitionCN: 期待好结果。optimistic 比 positive 窄，后者还覆盖赞同、证据与电荷。

entries.definition: saying yes or giving support. Affirmative matches sense 02 and is the formal opposite of negative.
entries.definitionCN: 说“是”或给予支持。affirmative 对应第 2 义项，是 negative 的正式反义。

entries.definition: sure about oneself or an outcome. Confident describes the feeling; positive can describe both the feeling and the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己或结果有把握。confident 描述感受；positive 既可指感受，也可指证据。

entries.definition: helpful and intended to improve something. Constructive fits sense 03 and stresses usefulness rather than mood.
entries.definitionCN: 有益且意在改进的。constructive 对应第 3 义项，强调有用性而非情绪。

entries.definition: clear and certain. Definite matches sense 04 and is close to the older core of positive.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而确定的。definite 对应第 4 义项，贴近 positive 较古老的核心义。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the plus side of the axis, the firm yes, the proof on the table, the test result, and the uncompared adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：轴的正侧、干脆的“是”、桌上的证据、化验结果、未作比较的形容词。

normal.en: Positive is the plus side: on a number line it points right, and in mood it points up.
normal.cn: positive 是加号那一边：在数轴上指向右，在心情上指向上。

normal.en: A positive answer is a yes that has been nailed down, not a maybe.
normal.cn: 肯定的答复是被钉死的“是”，不是“也许”。

normal.en: Positive proof is evidence placed on the table where nobody can talk it away.
normal.cn: 确凿证据就是摆到桌上、谁也说不掉的证据。

normal.en: A positive test means the thing you asked about is definitely there, like a light turning on.
normal.cn: 阳性检测意味着你问的那个东西确实在，就像一盏灯亮了。

normal.en: In grammar the positive degree is the plain form before any comparison touches it.
normal.cn: 语法上的原级，就是任何比较来碰它之前的朴素形式。

abstract.en: Positive originally meant settled by authority, not cheerful; the modern smile is a late guest in an old legal house.
abstract.cn: positive 本指“由权威定下”，并非“愉快”；现代的笑脸是这座古老法律宅子里晚来的客人。

abstract.en: A plus sign is a decision about direction, not a discovery about value.
abstract.cn: 加号是关于方向的决定，而不是关于价值的发现。

abstract.en: To call evidence positive is to say the question is closed; that is why the word can sound both reassuring and dangerous.
abstract.cn: 把证据称为 positive，等于宣布问题已经关闭；所以这个词听上去既可让人安心，也可让人警觉。

examples.en: The study found a positive correlation between sleep and test scores.
examples.cn: 这项研究发现睡眠与考试成绩之间存在正相关。

examples.en: Two of the samples tested positive for the bacteria.
examples.cn: 其中两份样本的细菌检测呈阳性。

examples.en: Try to frame the feedback in positive terms before listing the problems.
examples.cn: 在列举问题之前，尽量用正面措辞来组织反馈。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖则提夫”——把好处剖出来、提出来给大家看，就是 positive（积极的、正面的）

root: 拉丁语 ponere“放置”的过去分词 positus → positivus“经约定确定的” → 英语 positive（14 世纪，先用于法律与哲学）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is 'settled, laid down'. A settled answer is affirmative; settled evidence is proof; a settled direction on the axis is plus; a settled charge is positive; a settled outlook is optimism. The grammatical sense is simply the form before comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是“被确定、被定下”。确定下来的回答是肯定；确定下来的证据是确凿；轴上确定下来的方向是正；确定下来的电荷是正电；确定下来的看法是乐观。语法义则只是比较之前的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark placed firmly on the plus side of a line, with nothing left open.
core.cn: 核心意象：在一条线的正侧牢牢按下记号，不留任何悬而未决。

branches.en: CERTAINTY: the firm yes and the proof that closes the question.
branches.cn: 确定：干脆的“是”，以及关闭问题的证据。

branches.en: VALUE: the hopeful outlook and the good effect it expects.
branches.cn: 价值：乐观的心态，以及它所期待的良好效果。

branches.en: DIAGNOSIS: the test that finds the thing present.
branches.cn: 诊断：查出某物确实存在的检测。

branches.en: SIGN: the plus side of the number line and of the electric charge.
branches.cn: 符号：数轴与电荷的正侧。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the plain degree, stated before any comparison.
branches.cn: 语法：任何比较之前的朴素级。

intro.en: Positive is built from a Latin participle plus the adjective ending -ivus. The same stem, with different prefixes, yields most of the place-and-state vocabulary of English.
intro.cn: positive 由一个拉丁分词加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成。同一个词干配上不同前缀，产出了英语里大量表示“放置与状态”的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin positus is the pivot: every word below either contains it or is built by adding a prefix to the verb it comes from.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 positus 是枢纽：下面每个词要么含有它，要么是在其来源动词上加前缀构成。

items.meaning: tending toward, having the nature of
items.meaningCN: 倾向于；具有……性质的形容词后缀
表示状态或性质的名词后缀
表示学说或体系的词尾

latinEntries.meaningCN: 经约定确定的；约定俗成的

definition_zh: 拥有；具备；支配；附身
definition_en: to own something, to have a quality or ability, or to control a person's mind as a spirit does
core_image: 一只手按在椅背上，以主人身份稳稳坐定
scene: 拍卖行的灯已经调暗，木槌悬在半空，围观的人屏住呼吸。The collector possesses a small gold watch that once belonged to a railway engineer.
sceneCN: 这里 possess 是「拥有」（第 1 个义项：作为财产持有某物）；句意为这位收藏者拥有一只曾属于铁路工程师的小金表。画面里有调暗的灯、悬起的木槌和一只旧表。

pos.zh: 拥有；具备；支配；（鬼神）附身

collocations.zh: 你着了什么魔；你怎么会这样

derivatives.zh: possess 加表示「人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「拥有者；持有人」
possess 加 -ive 构成，义为「占有欲强的；所有格的」
self 与 possessed 复合，义为「沉着冷静的」，字面是「自我掌控的」

senses.title: To own something as property
senses.definition: to have something as your own property, especially something valuable or legally held
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为自己的财产持有，尤指贵重或依法持有的东西
senses.example: The family possesses two farms and a small orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人拥有两座农场和一小片果园。
senses.why: The Latin verb possidere pictured a master sitting over a place, so the earliest sense is holding property with authority rather than merely touching it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 possidere 的画面是主人坐在一处地方之上，所以最早的义项是带着支配意味地持有财产，而不只是碰到它。

senses.title: To have a quality or ability
senses.definition: to have a particular quality, skill or feature as part of what you are
senses.definitionCN: 作为自身的一部分而具备某种品质、技能或特征
senses.example: She possesses an unusual memory for faces.
senses.exampleCN: 她对人的面孔有非同寻常的记忆力。
senses.why: Once the word could hold a visible thing, it could hold an invisible one too: a quality is treated as something a person carries around.
senses.whyCN: 词一旦能「持有」看得见的东西，也就能「持有」看不见的东西：品质被看成人随身带着的一样东西。

senses.title: To take hold of someone's mind
senses.definition: of a feeling or idea, to fill someone's mind so strongly that it controls their behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪或念头强烈占据某人的心神，以至于左右其行为
senses.example: A wild hope possessed him as he read the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 读那封信时，一个狂热的希望攫住了他。
senses.why: The step from owning objects to owning a mind is short: whatever fills your thoughts is felt as having moved in and taken the chair.
senses.whyCN: 从占有物品转到占有一个人的心神，只差一小步：凡是填满你念头的东西，都会被感觉成搬了进来、坐上了主位。

senses.title: To enter and control a person, as a spirit
senses.definition: of a spirit or demon, to enter a person and control what they say and do
senses.definitionCN: 指鬼魂或恶魔进入人体，控制其言行
senses.example: In the story a restless ghost possesses the youngest daughter.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里，一个不安的鬼魂附上了最小的女儿。
senses.why: This is the literal picture behind the third sense: an outside power physically occupying a body, which was later borrowed as a metaphor for strong feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这是第三个义项背后的字面画面：一种外在力量实体般占据了身体，后来才被借去比喻强烈的情绪。

intro.en: Possess comes from a Latin verb that joins the idea of being able with the idea of sitting, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: possess 来自一个把「有能力」与「坐」合在一起的拉丁动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *poti- meant powerful or lord, and it is generally thought to lie behind the Latin words for ability and mastery.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 *poti- 表示「有力量的、主人」，拉丁语中表示能力与主宰的词都从它而来。

items.en: Latin joined potis, able or powerful, with sedere, to sit, making possidere, literally to sit as master over something.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 potis（有能力的、有权的）与 sedere（坐）合起来，构成 possidere，字面就是「以主人身份坐在某物之上」。

items.en: The noun possessio named both the act of holding and the thing held, and its stem possess- carried that meaning into the other forms of the family.
items.cn: 名词 possessio 既指持有的行为，也指被持有的东西，词干 possess- 把这一含义带进这一族的其他词形。

items.en: Old French possesser, recorded from the twelfth century, meant to own or to hold, and it entered English in the centuries after the Norman settlement.
items.cn: 古法语的 possesser 自十二世纪起有记录，意为拥有、持有，在诺曼人定居之后的几个世纪里进入英语。

items.en: Modern English kept the legal and everyday sense of owning, then extended the word to qualities a person has and to a spirit taking over a mind.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了法律与日常两种「拥有」义，再把词义扩展到人所具备的品质，以及鬼神占据一个人的心神。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the same Latin family of holding; the near-meaning group collects plainer verbs for having and keeping.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个表示「持有」的拉丁词族；近义组收更朴素地表示「有、留住」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun of state built on the same Latin stem, meaning the holding or the thing held.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词干上的名词，表示持有这一状态或被持有的东西。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who tends to hold on to things or people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容总想把人或物抓在手里的。

entries.definition: The person who holds or owns something.
entries.definitionCN: 持有或拥有某物的人。

entries.definition: To take property or land away from someone by force or law.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力或法律手段剥夺某人的财产或土地。

entries.definition: To have something as your property, the plainest verb for it.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物，是最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To have something in your hands or under your control.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拿在手里，或置于自己控制之下。

entries.definition: The most general verb for something being yours or being with you.
entries.definitionCN: 最笼统的「有」，表示某物属于你或在你身边。

normalIntro.en: The word holds together a Latin adjective of power, a verb of sitting, and two English suffixes that turn it into a person and a tendency.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把表示权力的拉丁形容词、表示坐的动词，以及两个把它变成「人」和「倾向」的英语后缀箍在一起。

normal.en: Potis in Latin meant able or powerful, and sedere meant to sit, so possidere was to sit as master over a thing.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 potis 意为有能力的、有权的，sedere 意为坐，所以 possidere 就是坐在某物之上当主人。

normal.en: The double s is real: possess keeps the s of the Latin stem possess-, so it is never written posses or posess.
normal.cn: 双写 s 是真实的：possess 保留了拉丁词干 possess- 的 s，所以绝不写成 posses 或 posess。

normal.en: Possessor swaps the verb ending for -or, the suffix for a person, and names the one who holds.
normal.cn: possessor 把动词词尾换成表示人的 -or，指的就是持有的人。

normal.en: Possessive adds -ive, the suffix of tendency, so it describes a person inclined to hold on.
normal.cn: possessive 加的是表示倾向的 -ive，形容一个人总想抓住不放。

normal.en: Self-possessed uses the same verb in the sense of controlling oneself, and means calm rather than wealthy.
normal.cn: self-possessed 用的是这个词「掌控自己」的一面，意思是从容镇定，而不是富有。

abstract.en: Picture a hand resting flat on a chair arm: owning begins as the confidence to sit down and stay.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平放在扶手椅上：拥有最初就是一种敢坐下来、不走的底气。

abstract.en: A quality you possess is something invisible that you carry the way you carry a key.
abstract.cn: 你具备的品质，是一件看不见却随身带着的东西，像口袋里的一把钥匙。

abstract.en: The jump from owning a house to being owned by a fear shows how quickly holding turns into being held.
abstract.cn: 从拥有一栋房子，到被一种恐惧攫住，说明「抓住」与「被抓住」之间只隔一层。

examples.en: The collector possesses a small gold watch from the last century.
examples.cn: 这位收藏者拥有一只上世纪的小金表。

examples.en: He possesses a patience that surprises his students.
examples.cn: 他的耐心让他的学生感到惊讶。

examples.en: A sudden doubt possessed her at the door.
examples.cn: 站在门口时，一阵突如其来的疑虑攫住了她。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕塞死」——东西太多，柜子快被塞死，因为样样都想拥有；记住 possess 是拥有。

root: 拉丁语 potis（有能力的、有权的）与 sedere（坐）合成 possidere（以主人身份坐定、占有），经古法语 possesser 进入英语；同族词都围绕「持有、掌控」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is holding something with authority; the senses then reach from property to invisible qualities, to a mind taken over, and finally to a spirit in possession of a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是带着支配意味地持有某物；义项由此从财物伸向看不见的品质，再伸向被占据的心神，最后落到鬼神占据身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand resting on the arm of a chair, a master sitting firmly in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在椅子的扶手上，主人稳稳坐定。

branches.en: a deed folded inside a wooden box
branches.cn: 折好放在木盒里的地契

branches.en: a voice that remembers every face
branches.cn: 记得每一张面孔的嗓音

branches.en: a hope that will not leave the room
branches.cn: 赖在房间里不肯走的希望

branches.en: a cold draft passing through a locked door
branches.cn: 穿过锁着的门的一股冷风

branches.en: two farms and a talent, both called someone's own
branches.cn: 两座农场与一种才能，都被说成某人的

intro.en: A Latin adjective of power, a verb of sitting, and English suffixes for a person and a tendency carry the whole word.
intro.cn: 一个表示权力的拉丁形容词、一个表示坐的动词，加上表示人和倾向的英语后缀，撑起了整个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is well recorded: potis, sedere, possidere and possessio all bear on this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族的拉丁词有明确记录：potis、sedere、possidere 与 possessio 都与这个词有关。

items.meaning: to sit as master, to hold
tending to, having the nature of

definition_zh: 拥有；所有物；属地；控球权
definition_en: the state of owning something, the things owned, territory held, or control of the ball in a game
core_image: 腰上挂着一串钥匙，走一步响一声
scene: 搬家那天箱子一只只打开，主人把每件旧物都擦了又擦。Her possessions filled three rooms of the new flat.
sceneCN: 这里 possession 是「所有物」（第 2 个义项：属于某人的东西）；句意为她的物品装满了新公寓的三个房间。画面里有搬家的纸箱和擦拭旧物的手。

pos.zh: 拥有；所有物；属地；控球权

derivatives.zh: dis-（剥夺）加 possess 构成，义为「剥夺……的财产或土地」
同一词干加 -ive，义为「占有欲强的；所有格的」
同一词干加表示人的 -or，义为「拥有者；持有人」

senses.title: The state of owning something
senses.definition: the state of having something as your own, especially when this is recognized by law
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为自己所有的状态，尤指得到法律承认的持有
senses.example: The house has been in the family's possession for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子由这个家族持有一个世纪了。
senses.why: The Latin noun named the act of holding before it named the object, so the abstract state comes first in English too.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词先指持有的行为，后指被持有的物件，所以英语里抽象的「持有状态」也排在前面。

senses.title: Something that you own
senses.definition: a thing that belongs to you, usually used in the plural for someone's personal belongings
senses.definitionCN: 属于你的东西，通常用复数指某人的个人财物
senses.example: She packed her few possessions into one bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己不多的几件东西装进一个袋子。
senses.why: From the state of holding, the word slides to the things held; the plural then becomes the usual way to list them one by one.
senses.whyCN: 从持有的状态滑向被持有的东西，复数形式随后成了把这些东西一件件清点出来的常用说法。

senses.title: Land or territory held by a country
senses.definition: a country or region controlled by another country, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 受另一国控制的国或地区，常用复数
senses.example: The empire's overseas possessions were costly to defend.
senses.exampleCN: 这个帝国的海外属地防卫起来代价高昂。
senses.why: Since possidere pictured mastery over a place, the political sense of land held by force or treaty grew straight out of that picture.
senses.whyCN: 既然 possidere 的画面就是对一处地方的主宰，靠武力或条约占有的土地这一政治义便直接从那幅画面里长出来。

senses.title: Control of the ball in a sport
senses.definition: in team sports, the time during which one side has the ball and controls play
senses.definitionCN: 在团队运动中，一方持球并控制比赛节奏的那段时间
senses.example: The home side had possession for most of the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在下半场大部分时间里控制着球。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal idea of holding: the side that holds the ball holds the game, so possession names a temporary kind of control.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了法律上的「持有」观念：持球的一方控制着比赛，于是 possession 用来指一种临时性的掌控。

intro.en: Possession is the noun built on the same Latin verb as possess, and it kept the whole range of that verb: holding, the thing held, and land held.
intro.cn: possession 是与 possess 同一个拉丁动词上的名词，完整保留了那个动词的范围：持有、被持有之物、被占有的土地。

items.en: Latin potis meant able or powerful, and it supplied the first element of the verb possidere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 potis 意为有能力的、有权的，它是动词 possidere 的前半部分。

items.en: Possidere combined potis with sedere, to sit, so that owning was pictured as sitting in command of a place.
items.cn: possidere 把 potis 与 sedere（坐）合成，于是拥有被想象成坐在一处地方发号施令。

items.en: The noun possessio covered the state of holding, the object held and land held, a range English took over almost whole.
items.cn: 名词 possessio 涵盖持有的状态、被持有的物件以及占有的土地，英语几乎整套接收了这一范围。

items.en: Anglo-Norman and Old French possession kept the same breadth, and legal French gave the word a firm place in English law.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼语与古法语的 possession 保留了同样的宽度，法律法语又让它在英国法中站稳了位置。

items.en: Modern English counts possessions in the plural for personal belongings, and uses the singular for territory and for control of the ball.
items.cn: 现代英语用复数 possessions 指个人财物，用单数指属地以及比赛中的控球权。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same holding family in its various forms; the near-meaning group gathers words for what a person owns.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个「持有」词族的不同词形；近义组收表示一个人所拥有之物的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to own or to hold.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，意为拥有、持有。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person or grammar form that claims ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 形容占有欲强的人，或表示所属关系的语法形式。

entries.definition: To strip someone of property or land.
entries.definitionCN: 剥夺某人的财产或土地。

entries.definition: The one who holds what the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 持有这个名词所指之物的人。

entries.definition: Things owned, especially land or buildings, and the right to them.
entries.definitionCN: 所拥有的东西，尤指土地房产及其权利。

entries.definition: The small personal things that someone carries or keeps.
entries.definitionCN: 某人随身携带或保存的个人小物件。

entries.definition: Something valuable that a person or company owns.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或公司拥有的有价值的东西。

normalIntro.en: The noun inherits a Latin verb about sitting as master, and its family spreads from a state of owning to the objects, the land, and even the ball.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词继承了一个「以主人身份坐定」的拉丁动词，词族从持有状态铺到物件、土地，甚至球。

normal.en: Potis meant able and sedere meant to sit, so the noun still carries the picture of a master seated over a place.
normal.cn: potis 意为有能力，sedere 意为坐，所以这个名词里仍坐着一位压住场子的主人。

normal.en: The suffix -ion turns the verb into the name of a state, so possession is the holding and not the holder.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ion 把动词变成状态的名字，所以 possession 是持有本身，而不是持有者。

normal.en: The plural possessions is the everyday word for the things scattered through your bags and rooms.
normal.cn: 复数 possessions 是日常说法，指散落在包里和房间里的那些东西。

normal.en: Dispossess adds dis-, away, and reverses the holding: the things are taken out of your hands.
normal.cn: dispossess 加上表示「离开」的 dis-，把持有反过来：东西被从你手里拿走。

normal.en: Legal English keeps possession for land and goods, which is why the word sounds formal in a courtroom.
normal.cn: 法律英语用 possession 指土地与货物，所以这个词在法庭上听起来很正式。

abstract.en: A ring of keys at the waist: each key is a possession, and the ring itself is possession.
abstract.cn: 腰间一串钥匙：每一把是一个所有物，而整串就是「拥有」本身。

abstract.en: Owning is a relation, not a thing, so one word can name both the state and the objects that fill it.
abstract.cn: 拥有是一种关系而不是一件东西，所以同一个词既能指状态，也能指填满这个状态的那些物件。

abstract.en: When a country calls a distant island a possession, the word quietly turns land and people into property.
abstract.cn: 当一个国家把远方岛屿称作 possession，这个词就悄悄把土地和人变成了财产。

examples.en: The old house came into her possession last spring.
examples.cn: 这栋老房子去年春天归她所有。

examples.en: He lost most of his possessions in the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水让他失去了大部分财物。

examples.en: The team kept possession and waited for an opening.
examples.cn: 球队保持控球，等待机会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕塞身」——家当太多，全塞在身上就走不动；记住 possession 是财物。

root: 与 possess 同源，出自拉丁动词 possidere（占有）的名词形式 possessio，词干 possess- 加 -ion；同族词围绕「持有者、被持有物、剥夺」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the state of holding; from it come the things held, the land a country holds, and the temporary holding of a ball.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是持有这一状态；由此分出被持有的东西、一国所占的土地，以及比赛里对球的临时持有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of keys at the waist that sounds with every step.
core.cn: 核心意象：腰间一串钥匙，每走一步就响一声。

branches.en: a deed that proves who may stay
branches.cn: 证明谁有权住下的地契

branches.en: a bag of worn clothes in a doorway
branches.cn: 门口一袋穿旧的衣服

branches.en: an island drawn in one colour on a map
branches.cn: 地图上被涂成一种颜色的岛

branches.en: ten seconds of passing before a shot
branches.cn: 出手前十秒的传导

branches.en: a watch kept for years and worn every day
branches.cn: 珍藏多年、天天佩戴的表

intro.en: The word is the noun of state from a Latin verb of mastery, and its endings mark a person, a tendency, and a reversal.
intro.cn: 这个词是那个表示主宰的拉丁动词的状态名词，它的词尾分别标出人、倾向和反转。

latinIntro.en: The noun rests on a recorded Latin verb and its noun possessio, with potis and sedere as the two elements inside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个名词依托有记录的拉丁动词及其名词 possessio，内部两个成分是 potis 与 sedere。

definition_zh: 可能性；可能的事；潜力
definition_en: the chance that something may happen, a possible event, or the capacity for future development
core_image: 一扇没上锁的门，门后还看不清
scene: 面试结束后，主管没有当场答复，只说还要再议一次。There is a real possibility that the job will go to another candidate.
sceneCN: 这里 possibility 是「可能性」（第 1 个义项：某事可能发生）；句意为这份工作很可能落到另一位候选人手里。画面里有面试桌和未落笔的记录纸。

pos.zh: 可能性；可能的事；潜力

derivatives.zh: 源自拉丁 possibilis，义为「可能的」
possible 加 -ly，义为「也许；可能」
im-（不）加 possible，义为「不可能的」

senses.title: The chance that something may happen
senses.definition: the fact that something may happen or may be true, without certainty
senses.definitionCN: 某事可能发生或可能为真，但并不确定
senses.example: There is a real possibility that the flight will be delayed.
senses.exampleCN: 航班延误的可能性确实存在。
senses.why: The word starts from Latin posse, to be able: what is possible is what can come to be, so the core sense is an open future rather than a fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始于拉丁语 posse（能够）：可能的就是能够出现的，所以核心义是一个尚未关闭的未来，而不是既成事实。

senses.title: A possible event or result
senses.definition: a single thing that may happen, or one of several results you can imagine
senses.definitionCN: 某一件可能发生的事，或你能设想到的若干结果之一
senses.example: We must prepare for several possibilities before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会前我们必须为几种可能的情况做准备。
senses.why: If possibility is the open future in general, counting those openings turns the abstract quality into separate items on a list.
senses.whyCN: 如果 possibility 泛指未定的未来，那么把这些开口一个个数出来，抽象性质就变成清单上分开的条目。

senses.title: The chance to develop or succeed
senses.definition: the opportunities a person, place or plan has for future growth, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 人、地方或计划在未来成长上的机会，常用复数
senses.example: The young player still has great possibilities.
senses.exampleCN: 这名年轻球员仍有很大的发展潜力。
senses.why: An unwritten future can belong to a person as well as to an event, and then the word points to unused capacity rather than to sheer chance.
senses.whyCN: 未被写定的未来既属于事件，也属于人；这时词义指向尚未用上的能力，而不是纯粹的偶然。

intro.en: Possibility comes from Latin posse, to be able, and it reached English through the adjective possibilis and the noun possibilitas before French passed it on.
intro.cn: possibility 来自拉丁语 posse（能够），先有形容词 possibilis 与名词 possibilitas，再由法语传给英语。

items.en: Latin posse, to be able, is generally analysed as potis, able, plus esse, to be, so ability was phrased as being in a position to be.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 posse（能够）由 potis（有能力的）加 esse（是、存在）构成，能力被说成「处于能够存在的状态」。

items.en: The adjective possibilis described something that can be or can happen, adding -bilis, the suffix of capability.
items.cn: 形容词 possibilis 描述能够存在或能够发生的事物，加的是表示「能够被……」的后缀 -bilis。

items.en: Late Latin coined possibilitas for the quality of being possible, a noun built on the adjective rather than on the verb.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语造出 possibilitas 表示「可能」这一性质，这个名词建立在形容词而非动词之上。

items.en: Old French possibilité passed the word to English, where it first named the abstract quality before it named concrete chances.
items.cn: 古法语的 possibilité 把词传给英语，它先指抽象的性质，之后才指具体的机会。

items.en: Modern English uses possibility for a chance, for a single possible event, and for the untapped powers a person or a plan may hold.
items.cn: 现代英语用 possibility 指机会、指单件可能发生的事，也指人或计划尚未发挥的潜力。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same Latin adjective of capability; the near-meaning group gathers words for chance and for what may come.
note.cn: 形近组建立在同一个表示「能够」的拉丁形容词上；近义组收表示机会与未来之事的词。

entries.definition: The adjective that says something can be or can happen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，表示某事能够存在或发生。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning perhaps or in a way that can be done.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，表示也许，或以可行的方式。

entries.definition: Not able to be or to happen, formed with the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀构成，表示不可能存在或发生。

entries.definition: The negative noun that mirrors this word exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 与这个词完全对应的否定名词。

entries.definition: How likely it is that something will happen.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能程度。

entries.definition: The measured probability that something will occur.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事发生概率的衡量。

entries.definition: Something that may happen in the future, often hoped for.
entries.definitionCN: 未来可能发生的事，常指所期望的。

entries.definition: The ability or quality that exists but is not yet used.
entries.definitionCN: 已存在但尚未发挥的能力或特质。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from the Latin verb for being able, and its family keeps returning to capability, chance and what has not yet happened.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「能够」的拉丁动词构成，词族反复回到能力、机会以及尚未发生的事。

normal.en: Posse, to be able, is analysed as potis plus esse, able plus to be, so possibility is literally a way of being that can still arrive.
normal.cn: posse（能够）可分析为 potis 加 esse，即「有能力」加「存在」，所以 possibility 字面上是一种还可能到来的存在方式。

normal.en: The suffix -bilis marks what can be done or can exist, and it is the same ending hidden in visible and flexible.
normal.cn: 后缀 -bilis 标出「能够被做成或能够存在」的东西，visible 与 flexible 里藏的也是这个结尾。

normal.en: The ending -ity turns the adjective possible into the noun possibility, naming the quality itself.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ity 把形容词 possible 变成名词 possibility，命名的是这种性质本身。

normal.en: The plural possibilities often means chances to develop, as in the possibilities of a young player.
normal.cn: 复数 possibilities 常指发展的机会，例如一名年轻球员的可能性。

normal.en: Impossible adds im-, not, to possible, and impossibility mirrors possibility with the same negative prefix.
normal.cn: impossible 在 possible 前加表示否定的 im-，impossibility 也用同一个否定前缀与 possibility 对应。

abstract.en: An unlocked door with the room still dark: that is possibility before it hardens into an event.
abstract.cn: 一扇没锁的门，屋里还黑着：这就是尚未变成事件之前的可能性。

abstract.en: A list of possible results is simply the open future cut into countable pieces.
abstract.cn: 一张可能结果的清单，不过是被切成可数碎片的开放未来。

abstract.en: To say a person is full of possibilities is to say the future has not spent itself on them yet.
abstract.cn: 说一个人充满可能性，意思是未来还没有在他身上用完。

examples.en: There is a real possibility that the flight will be delayed.
examples.cn: 航班延误的可能性确实存在。

examples.en: We must prepare for several possibilities before the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会前我们必须为几种可能的情况做准备。

examples.en: The young player still has great possibilities.
examples.cn: 这名年轻球员仍有很大的发展潜力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕是必能」——凡事都想着「怕是也能」，就是给自己留了一种可能；possibility 是可能性。

root: 拉丁语 posse（能够）通常分析为 potis（有能力的）加 esse（是、存在），再由 possibilis（可能的）与晚期拉丁 possibilitas 发展而来；它与 possess 一族共享 potis，但走的是「能够」这一条线。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an outcome that can still happen; the senses then count single possible events and, finally, point at powers not yet used.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个仍可能发生的结果；义项由此数出单件可能之事，最后指向尚未用上的能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unlocked door with the room beyond still in darkness.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇没有上锁的门，门后的房间还在暗处。

branches.en: a letter that may or may not arrive
branches.cn: 可能来也可能不来的信

branches.en: three routes drawn on a napkin
branches.cn: 餐巾纸上画出的三条路线

branches.en: a young voice still finding its range
branches.cn: 还在找音域的年轻嗓音

branches.en: a delay announced but not yet dated
branches.cn: 宣布了却还没定日期的延误

branches.en: two futures folded into one name
branches.cn: 折在同一个名字里的两种未来

intro.en: A Latin verb of being able, its adjective of capability, and the noun endings that name a quality hold the word together.
intro.cn: 一个表示「能够」的拉丁动词、它的能力形容词，以及命名性质的名词词尾，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are recorded: posse, possibilis and possibilitas, with potis as the element shared with the possess family.
latinIntro.cn: 这些拉丁词形都有记录：posse、possibilis 与 possibilitas，其中 potis 是与 possess 一族共有的成分。

definition_zh: 可能的；能做到的；很可能的；合适的；尽可能好的
definition_en: able to be done or to happen; likely but not certain; suitable in the circumstances
core_image: 一扇没有上锁的门：门后有路，但还没有人迈出去
scene: 面试结束后，年轻人站在公司门口，反复回想自己还有没有机会。The recruiter said a second interview was possible if the first one went well.
sceneCN: 这里是「有可能的」（第 1 个义项：事情能够发生）；句意为招聘人员说，如果初面顺利，二面是有可能的。画面里可留意的是那扇半开的门和候选人握着的手。

pos.zh: 可能的；能做到的；很可能的；合适的

derivatives.zh: possible 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，指「可能性」，-ity 把形容词变成抽象名词
possible 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，表示「也许；可能地」
否定前缀 im- 加 possible 构成，表示「不可能的」

senses.title: Able to be done or achieved
senses.definition: able to happen or be done, because nothing stands in the way
senses.definitionCN: 因为不存在阻碍，所以能够发生或做到
senses.example: A cure for the disease may be possible within ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年之内或许有可能找到这种病的疗法。
senses.why: The Latin verb posse means to be able; the first sense is bare ability with no obstacle in front of it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 posse 意为「能够」，所以这个词最初的义项就是「有能力、又没阻碍」。

senses.title: Likely to be true or to happen
senses.definition: having a strong chance of being true or of happening, though not certain
senses.definitionCN: 成真或发生的几率很大，但并不确定
senses.example: It is possible that the train will be late again.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟火车很可能再次晚点。
senses.why: Once a thing can happen, the same word is used for what a speaker judges will probably happen, so ability shades into likelihood.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然能够发生，说话人就用同一个词来表达自己判断「大概会发生」，于是「能力」之外又添了「几率」。

senses.title: Suitable in a particular situation
senses.definition: acceptable or suitable for a purpose or a person, given the limits of the situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情境的限制下，对某个目的或某个人来说是合适、可接受的
senses.example: She is the only possible candidate for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这份工作唯一合适的人选。
senses.why: If something can be done, it can also be chosen; the word then judges fitness instead of bare ability.
senses.whyCN: 一件事只要做得到，就可以被选中，于是这个词从「能不能」转为评判「合不合适」。

senses.title: As good as the situation allows
senses.definition: used after a superlative or with all, meaning the best that the circumstances permit
senses.definitionCN: 用于最高级之后或与 all 连用，表示在现有条件下能达到的最好程度
senses.example: We gave the visitors the best possible welcome.
senses.exampleCN: 我们给了来访者尽可能好的接待。
senses.why: When ability is stretched to its limit, possible stops meaning merely can and starts marking the ceiling of what can be reached.
senses.whyCN: 当「能够」被推到极限，possible 就不再只是「可以」，而是标出「能达到的上限」。

intro.en: Possible comes from Latin posse, to be able, whose stem joins an old word for power with the verb to be.
intro.cn: possible 出自拉丁语 posse（能够），其词干由表示「有力量」的古老词与动词「是」组合而成。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning powerful or able, usually written *poti-, is generally thought to lie behind the Latin family.
items.cn: 一般认为，表示「有力量、有能力」的重构词根 *poti- 是拉丁这一族词的远祖。

items.en: Latin potis meant able, capable or powerful, and it combined with esse, to be, to build the verb of ability.
items.cn: 拉丁语 potis 意为「有能力的、有力量的」，它与 esse（是）结合，构成表示「能够」的动词。

items.en: From posse Latin formed the adjective possibilis, meaning that which can be done or can exist.
items.cn: 拉丁语由 posse 造出形容词 possibilis，意为「做得到的、能够存在的」。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as possible and passed it to English, keeping the sense of what can be or can happen.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 possible 并传入英语，保留了「能够存在或发生」的意思。

items.en: English added -ity for the abstract noun, -ly for the adverb and im- for the negative, so one Latin stem now covers a small family.
items.cn: 英语后来加上 -ity 构成抽象名词、加 -ly 构成副词、加 im- 构成否定式，同一个拉丁词干如今撑起了一个小词族。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same Latin verb of ability; the second collects words that also talk about what may happen.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「能够」词族上的词；近义组收同样谈论「也许会发生」的词。

entries.definition: The adverb built from possible with -ly, meaning perhaps.
entries.definitionCN: 由 possible 加 -ly 构成的副词，意为「也许」。

entries.definition: Not able to happen or be done, formed with the negative prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀 im- 构成，意为「不可能的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the chance that something may exist or happen.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事存在或发生的「可能性」的名词。

entries.definition: Powerful or effective, from the same old word for able that feeds posse.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「强有力的」，与 posse 同出表示「有能力」的古老词。

entries.definition: Expected to happen or probably true.
entries.definitionCN: 预期会发生或大概是真的。

entries.definition: Strongly likely, more confident than merely possible.
entries.definitionCN: 很有可能，语气比 possible 更确定。

entries.definition: Able to be carried out in practice, with the means available.
entries.definitionCN: 在现有条件下能够实际做到的。

entries.definition: Able to be imagined or believed, however unlikely.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被想象或相信的，尽管可能性很小。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of ability, and its family keeps adding endings that turn ability into a noun, an adverb or its opposite.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「能够」的动词上，同族词不断加后缀，把「能力」变成名词、副词或它的反面。

normal.en: Posse in Latin means to be able, so anything possible is something you are able to do.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为「能够」，所以 possible 就是「做得到的事」。

normal.en: Potis, the old word for able, also hides inside potent and potential, so power runs through the whole family.
normal.cn: 表示「有能力」的古词 potis 也藏在 potent 与 potential 里，力量贯穿整个词族。

normal.en: Add -ity to possible and the chance itself becomes a noun: possibility.
normal.cn: 在 possible 后加 -ity，机会本身就变成名词 possibility。

normal.en: Add im- to possible and the ability disappears: impossible.
normal.cn: 在 possible 前加 im-，能力就消失，成了 impossible。

normal.en: The phrase as soon as possible keeps the old sense of ability pressed against a deadline.
normal.cn: 短语 as soon as possible 把古老的「能力」之意压到一个截止时间上。

abstract.en: A door that is not locked is possible; whether anyone walks through it is a separate question.
abstract.cn: 门没上锁，这叫 possible；有没有人走进去，是另一回事。

abstract.en: Possible marks the edge of the map rather than a road already travelled.
abstract.cn: possible 标的是地图的边缘，而不是已经走过的路。

abstract.en: Every finished thing was once only possible, which is why the word keeps a hint of the future.
abstract.cn: 每件完成的事当初都只是 possible，所以这个词总带着一点未来的气味。

examples.en: Is it possible to finish the report by Friday?
examples.cn: 有可能在周五前完成报告吗？

examples.en: The doctors did everything possible to save him.
examples.cn: 医生们为救他做了一切能做的事。

examples.en: A peaceful solution is still possible.
examples.cn: 和平解决仍然是有可能的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕谁保」——怕谁保不住，事情就只好说「有可能」；记住 possible 表示可能的。

root: 拉丁语 posse（能够）← potis（有能力的）+ esse（是）；同族词多与「能力、可能」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is ability without obstruction; from there the word spreads to likelihood, to fitness for a purpose, and to the upper limit of what can be reached.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「有能力、无阻碍」；由此分出「可能性大小」「是否合适」，以及「能达到的上限」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door left unlocked, with a path visible behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇没有上锁的门，门后能看见一条路。

branches.en: a locked door that someone finally opens
branches.cn: 一扇终于被人打开的锁着的门

branches.en: a forecast that says rain is likely by evening
branches.cn: 预报说傍晚大概有雨

branches.en: a shortlist with only one suitable name on it
branches.cn: 名单上只剩一个合适的人

branches.en: a welcome pushed to its warmest
branches.cn: 把欢迎做到最热烈

branches.en: a seed that may or may not sprout
branches.cn: 一粒可能发芽也可能不发芽的种子

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin verb of ability, its older root of power, a suffix of possibility, and English endings that reverse or redirect it.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「能够」动词、更早的「力量」词根、表示「可……的」后缀，以及英语中表示否定与副词的后缀共同构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse, potis and possibilis supply the core; the English family grows by prefix and suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 posse、potis、possibilis 提供核心，英语这一族靠前缀与后缀继续生长。

definition_zh: 也许；可能地；（与 can、could 连用）究竟；能否
definition_en: perhaps; used with can or could to stress surprise or doubt, or to make a request sound polite
core_image: 一盏忽明忽暗的灯：会不会亮，此刻还说不准
scene: 朋友问周末要不要去爬山，她看了看窗外的乌云，没有马上答应。The sky may possibly clear up by Saturday morning.
sceneCN: 这里是「也许」（第 1 个义项：表示不确定）；句意为到周六早上天色也许会放晴。画面可留意的是窗外压低的云和那盏还没开的灯。

pos.zh: 也许；可能地；（用于强调或委婉请求）

derivatives.zh: possibly 加否定前缀 im- 构成，表示「不可能地；难以想象地」
possibly 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，表示「可能的」
同一词族的名词形式，表示「可能性」

senses.title: Perhaps; it may be so
senses.definition: used to say that something may be true or may happen, but is not certain
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事也许是真的，或者也许会发生，但并不确定
senses.example: She will possibly arrive before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她也许中午前会到。
senses.why: The adverb carries the adjective's sense of ability into a judgement the speaker will not fully commit to.
senses.whyCN: 副词把形容词「能够」的意思带进一句说话人不敢完全担保的判断里，说的就是「也许」。

senses.title: Used with can or could for emphasis
senses.definition: used after can or could to show surprise, doubt or strong feeling about whether something is possible
senses.definitionCN: 用在 can 或 could 之后，对某事是否可能表示惊讶、怀疑或强烈语气
senses.example: How could she possibly forget the keys again?
senses.exampleCN: 她怎么可能又把钥匙忘了？
senses.why: If ability is stressed to its limit, a neutral question turns into a challenge to belief.
senses.whyCN: 把「能力」强调到极限，原本中性的问句就变成了对「这怎么可能」的质疑。

senses.title: Used to make a polite request
senses.definition: used in questions such as could you possibly to make a request sound careful and polite
senses.definitionCN: 用于 could you possibly 这类问句，使请求显得客气、留有余地
senses.example: Could you possibly send me the file today?
senses.exampleCN: 您今天能不能把文件发给我？
senses.why: Asking whether someone even has the ability to help softens the demand and leaves an easy way to refuse.
senses.whyCN: 先问对方「有没有可能帮上」，请求就变软了，也给对方留了容易拒绝的余地。

intro.en: Possibly is the adverb of possible, and both go back to the Latin verb posse, to be able.
intro.cn: possibly 是 possible 的副词，两者都追溯到拉丁语动词 posse（能够）。

items.en: Potis, an old Latin adjective for able or powerful, combined with esse, to be, to yield the verb of ability.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 potis 表示「有能力的、有力量的」，它与 esse（是）结合，产生了表示「能够」的动词。

items.en: Posse meant to be able, and from it Latin built possibilis, that which can be done.
items.cn: posse 意为「能够」，拉丁语由它造出 possibilis，即「做得到的」。

items.en: Old French used possible for what can be or can happen, and English borrowed the adjective in this form.
items.cn: 古法语用 possible 表示「能够存在或发生的」，英语以这个形式借入了形容词。

items.en: Middle English possible described what is within reach or within reason, close to its modern meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语的 possible 指「做得到、说得通」的事，与现代义已经很接近。

items.en: English added the adverb ending -ly to the adjective, giving possibly, which marks an unsure judgement rather than an ability.
items.cn: 英语给这个形容词加上副词词尾 -ly，造出 possibly，用来标记没有把握的判断，而不是单纯的能力。

note.en: The first group follows the same Latin stem through its adjective, negative and noun forms; the second follows the meaning of uncertainty.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一拉丁词干看它的形容词、否定式与名词形式；近义组则沿「不确定」这条意义线展开。

entries.definition: The adjective that possibly is built from, meaning able to be or happen.
entries.definitionCN: possibly 所由构成的形容词，意为「可能的」。

entries.definition: Not able to happen or be done, with the negative prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀 im-，意为「不可能的」。

entries.definition: The noun naming the chance that something may be or happen.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事可能存在或发生的「可能性」的名词。

entries.definition: The negative adverb, used of things too difficult to imagine.
entries.definitionCN: 否定副词，用于难以想象地困难的事物。

entries.definition: A neutral word for maybe, common in careful speech.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的「也许」，在谨慎的表述中很常见。

entries.definition: A plainer, more conversational way to say perhaps.
entries.definitionCN: 更口语、更朴素的「也许」。

entries.definition: More likely than not, a stronger claim than possibly.
entries.definitionCN: 多半如此，语气比 possibly 更肯定。

entries.definition: In a way that can be imagined, however slight the chance.
entries.definitionCN: 在可以想象的范围内，不论机会多小。

normalIntro.en: The word is an adjective of ability turned into an adverb, so its endings carry most of its history.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「能够」的形容词转为副词，它的历史大半写在词尾上。

normal.en: Possibly is possible plus -ly, the ordinary English way of turning an adjective into an adverb.
normal.cn: possibly 就是 possible 加 -ly，这是英语把形容词变成副词最普通的方式。

normal.en: The -ly ending adds no doubt of its own; the uncertainty already sits inside possible.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 本身并不带来怀疑，不确定早就藏在 possible 里。

normal.en: Impossibly adds im- to possibly and closes the door: not even able to be imagined.
normal.cn: impossibly 在 possibly 前加 im-，把门关死，意为「连想都不可能」。

normal.en: In could you possibly, the adverb stretches ability into politeness rather than doubt.
normal.cn: 在 could you possibly 里，这个副词把「能力」拉长成客气，而不是怀疑。

normal.en: The double s in the spelling marks the Latin stem pos-se, which also shows in possible and impossible.
normal.cn: 拼写里的双写 s 标出拉丁词干 pos-se，在 possible 与 impossible 里同样出现。

abstract.en: Possibly is the word for leaving a door ajar without promising to walk through it.
abstract.cn: possibly 是「把门留着缝，却不保证走进去」时用的词。

abstract.en: A forecast lives on possibly: it names a chance rather than a fact.
abstract.cn: 天气预报就活在 possibly 上：它给的是机会，不是事实。

abstract.en: Saying possibly moves the weight of proof away from the speaker and onto the future.
abstract.cn: 说 possibly，就把举证的分量从说话人身上推给了未来。

examples.en: The meeting will possibly be moved to Thursday.
examples.cn: 会议也许会被改到周四。

examples.en: Could you possibly lend me your notes?
examples.cn: 你能不能把笔记借给我？

examples.en: She is possibly the best player on the team.
examples.cn: 她也许是队里最好的球员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕谁不力」——怕谁不肯出力，事情就只能说「也许」；记住 possibly 表示可能地。

root: possibly 由 possible 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，词干回到拉丁语 posse（能够）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an unsure maybe; the same adverb then hardens into emphatic disbelief and softens into a polite request.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是不确定的「也许」；同一个副词既能加重成质疑，也能放软成客气的请求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp that flickers, so nobody can say yet whether the room will be lit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏忽明忽暗的灯，房间会不会亮起来，此刻没人说得准。

branches.en: a forecast that keeps changing its mind
branches.cn: 一份反复改口的预报

branches.en: a friend asking how such a thing could ever happen
branches.cn: 朋友追问这种事怎么可能发生

branches.en: a carefully worded request left open to refusal
branches.cn: 一句留好退路的请求

branches.en: a rumour that nobody can confirm
branches.cn: 一则没人能证实的传闻

branches.en: a question mark placed before a favour
branches.cn: 在请求前放一个问号

intro.en: The word is an adjective of ability plus the English adverb ending, and its family adds a negative prefix and a noun suffix around the same Latin stem.
intro.cn: 这个词是「能够」的形容词加英语副词词尾构成，词族在同一拉丁词干周围再加否定前缀与名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse and possibilis carry the core meaning; the English adverb ending does the grammatical work.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 posse 与 possibilis 承载核心意义，英语副词词尾负责语法功能。

definition_zh: 邮政；邮件；职位；柱子；邮寄；张贴；发布
definition_en: the mail service or the mail itself; a job; an upright pole; to send by mail or to put a message where people can see it
core_image: 一根木桩立在路边，桩上钉着一块写满消息的木板
scene: 村口的老木门上贴着一张寻物启事，路过的人都停下脚步看。Someone had posted a notice about a lost dog on the gate.
sceneCN: 这里是「张贴、发布」（第 5 个义项：把消息公开出来）；句意为有人在门上贴了一张寻狗启事。画面里可留意木桩、旧门和那张被风掀起的纸。

pos.zh: 邮政；邮件；职位；柱子
邮寄；张贴；发布

derivatives.zh: post 加表示费用的后缀 -age 构成，指「邮费」
post 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，表示「邮政的」
post（张贴）加 -er 构成，原指张贴的告示，现多指「海报」

senses.title: The mail service and the letters it carries
senses.definition: the system that collects and delivers letters and parcels, or those letters and parcels themselves
senses.definitionCN: 收寄并投递信件、包裹的系统，也指这些信件与包裹本身
senses.example: The cheque came by post this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 支票是今天上午邮寄到的。
senses.why: Post first named a relay station where horses were changed; the letters that travelled from station to station took the name, and then the whole service did.
senses.whyCN: post 最初指换马的驿站；一站一站传下去的信件借用了这个名称，最后整套邮政系统也沿用了它。

senses.title: A job or position in an organization
senses.definition: a job in an organization, especially one with a title and fixed duties
senses.definitionCN: 组织中的一个职位，尤指有头衔、职责固定者
senses.example: She applied for a post in the finance department.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了财务部的一个职位。
senses.why: A post was also a place where a soldier or official was stationed, so the word slid from the spot to the duty held at that spot.
senses.whyCN: post 也指士兵或官员驻扎的地点，词义便从「那个位置」滑到「在那个位置上承担的职务」。

senses.title: An upright pole set in the ground
senses.definition: a strong upright piece of wood or metal fixed in the ground, used to support something or mark a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 固定在地里的坚固木柱或金属柱，用来支撑物件或标示界线
senses.example: A wooden post marks the end of the path.
senses.exampleCN: 一根木桩标出了小路的尽头。
senses.why: This is the oldest line of all: Latin postis named a doorpost or upright beam, and English kept the solid object.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一条线：拉丁语 postis 指门柱或直立的梁木，英语保留了这件实物本身。

senses.title: To send a letter or parcel by mail
senses.definition: to send a letter, parcel or message through the postal system
senses.definitionCN: 通过邮政系统寄出信件、包裹或消息
senses.example: I posted the documents to the embassy yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 我昨天把文件寄给了大使馆。
senses.why: Once post named the mail service, the noun turned into a verb: to post something is to hand it over to that service.
senses.whyCN: post 既然指邮政系统，名词就顺势转为动词，表示「把东西交给这套系统」。

senses.title: To put a notice or message where people can see it
senses.definition: to put up a notice in public, or to publish a message, picture or piece of writing online
senses.definitionCN: 把通知张贴在公共处，或在网上发布消息、图片、文字
senses.example: The school posted the exam results on its website.
senses.exampleCN: 学校把考试成绩发布在网站上。
senses.why: A post is a fixed place; to post something was to fix it there for everyone to read, and the internet reused the same picture for a screen.
senses.whyCN: post 是一个固定的位置；把东西 post 出来就是把它固定在那里让人人可读，网络时代把这幅画面搬到了屏幕上。

intro.en: Two Latin lines meet in this short word: postis, an upright beam, and posta, a station on a road, which itself comes from ponere, to place.
intro.cn: 两条拉丁线索在这个短词里汇合：postis 是直立的梁柱，posta 是路上的驿站，而 posta 又出自 ponere（放置）。

items.en: Postis meant a doorpost or upright beam, and this line alone gives English the wooden pole.
items.cn: postis 意为门柱或直立的梁木，仅这一条线就给了英语「木柱」这个义项。

items.en: The mail line starts elsewhere: ponere meant to put or place, and its participle positus, placed, stands behind the later station word.
items.cn: 邮政那条线另有起点：ponere 意为放置，它的过去分词 positus（被放置的）是后来「驿站」一词的背后形式。

items.en: Posta named a station on a road where horses and messengers were changed, a place where things were set down.
items.cn: posta 指路上换马、换信使的站点，也就是把人和物「安置下来」的地方。

items.en: English borrowed the French form poste for the riders and the letters, so post came to mean the mail and the office that handled it.
items.cn: 英语借入法语形式 poste，指骑马送信的人和信件，于是 post 兼指邮件与经办邮件的机构。

items.en: Modern English keeps both lines apart: the beam stays a post, while the station line grows into job posts, posting a letter and posting online.
items.cn: 现代英语把两条线分开保留：梁柱仍是 post，而「驿站」一线则长出职位、寄信与网络发布。

note.en: The first group collects words built on post with different endings; the second collects words for mail, for jobs and for poles, the three fields this word covers.
note.cn: 形近组收在 post 上加不同词尾构成的词；近义组收邮件、职位、柱子这三片词义场里的词。

entries.definition: The charge for sending mail, built with the suffix -age.
entries.definitionCN: 加后缀 -age 构成，指寄邮件所需的「邮费」。

entries.definition: Relating to the mail service, built with -al.
entries.definitionCN: 加后缀 -al 构成，表示「邮政的」。

entries.definition: A printed sheet put up for people to see, from the verb post.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词 post 而来，指张贴出来供人观看的印刷品「海报」。

entries.definition: A card sent by mail without an envelope.
entries.definitionCN: 不装信封、直接邮寄的「明信片」。

entries.definition: Letters and parcels, or the system that carries them.
entries.definitionCN: 信件与包裹，或运送它们的系统。

entries.definition: A job or rank held in an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 在组织中担任的职务或职位。

entries.definition: A tall upright support, often of stone.
entries.definitionCN: 高而直立的支撑物，常为石制。

entries.definition: To make writing or information available to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 把文字或信息公之于众。

normalIntro.en: Two Latin sources feed one spelling, and the senses sort themselves by which source they come from.
normalIntro.cn: 两条拉丁来源喂给同一个拼写，各个义项按来源自然分成两堆。

normal.en: The mail sense grows from posta, a relay station; letters moved from station to station along the road.
normal.cn: 邮政义出自 posta（驿站）；信件沿着大路一站一站往前传。

normal.en: The pole sense grows from postis, a doorpost, and has nothing to do with mail.
normal.cn: 柱子义出自 postis（门柱），与邮件毫无关系。

normal.en: Postage and postal keep the mail line, both built on post with different suffixes.
normal.cn: postage 与 postal 都留在邮政这条线上，只是加了不同后缀。

normal.en: A poster was first something posted up for people to read, before it meant a printed picture.
normal.cn: poster 最初指「张贴出来供人阅读的东西」，后来才指印刷的海报。

normal.en: To post a comment online repeats the old act of fixing a notice where others can see it.
normal.cn: 在网上 post 一条评论，重复的正是把告示固定在人人都看得见的地方。

abstract.en: One short word holds a wooden pole and a worldwide mail service because both are things set in a fixed place.
abstract.cn: 一个短词同时装着一根木桩和一套全球邮政，因为两者都是「被安置在固定位置」的东西。

abstract.en: A job post is a station for a person, just as a post was a station for a horse.
abstract.cn: 职位是人驻守的站点，正如当年的驿站是马匹换乘的站点。

abstract.en: Posting online is the village notice board moved onto a screen.
abstract.cn: 网络发布就是把村口的告示板搬到了屏幕上。

examples.en: Please post the letter before noon.
examples.cn: 请在中午前把信寄出去。

examples.en: He has held the post of manager for five years.
examples.cn: 他担任经理一职已经五年。

examples.en: A tall post supports the wire fence.
examples.cn: 一根高高的木桩撑着铁丝围栏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖斯特」——把邮包剖开再送出去；记住 post 既指邮寄，也指柱子。

root: 两条拉丁来源：postis（门柱、直立的梁木）给「柱子」；posta（驿站）及其背后的 ponere（放置）给「邮政、职位」。

sensesIntro.en: The pole is the older physical sense; the station line then yields mail, the job held at a place, and finally the act of making something public.
sensesIntro.cn: 「柱子」是更早的实物义；「驿站」一线则长出邮件、驻守的职位，最后长出「公之于众」的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden stake by the road with a message nailed to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：路边一根木桩，上面钉着一块写着消息的木板。

branches.en: a wooden stake holding up a fence
branches.cn: 木桩撑起一段栅栏

branches.en: a bag of letters moving from town to town
branches.cn: 一袋信件在城镇间传递

branches.en: a nameplate fixed on an office door
branches.cn: 固定在办公室门上的名牌

branches.en: a stamped envelope dropped into a box

intro.en: Two Latin sources meet here: postis, an upright beam, and posta, a station on a road, itself from ponere, to place.
intro.cn: 这个词有两条拉丁来源：postis 是直立的梁柱，posta 是路上的驿站，而 posta 又出自 ponere（放置）。

latinIntro.en: The Latin nouns postis and posta, with the verb ponere behind the second, explain both the pole and the mail.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 postis 与 posta 分别解释了「柱子」与「邮政」，后者背后还有动词 ponere。
